title: Pediatric Cardiology Fellowship

prerequisites.detail: Medical-school-level cardiovascular anatomy/physiology, pediatric history/physical examination concepts, basic ECG vocabulary, and evidence appraisal. The intended academic level is pediatrics resident/fellow or supervised clinician; other learners may use it only as non-clinical education.

No learner may use this course to interpret a patient study independently, make a treatment/transfer decision, prescribe, perform procedures, or claim competence. Clinical participation requires the learner’s own institution, supervisor, privileges, and policies.
ABP eligibility prerequisites are stated separately in boardEligibilityNotice and are not satisfied by these recommended academic prerequisites.

objectives: Apply a physiology-first framework to congenital and acquired pediatric cardiovascular presentations.
Map study topics to the ABP’s published 21-domain pediatric cardiology blueprint and universal tasks.
Interpret the scope and limits of ECG, echocardiography, fetal imaging, catheterization, and cross-sectional imaging questions.
Describe congenital anatomy, single-ventricle, arrhythmia, myocardial, vascular, acquired-inflammatory, inherited, and transition domains using uncertainty-aware language.
Critically appraise public evidence, licenses, and real-case provenance; communicate findings without patient-specific directives.
Design a systems/QI or scholarly question while distinguishing self-study from supervised fellowship practice.

units.title: Normal cardiovascular structure, physiology, and developmental reasoning
objectives: Relate fetal-to-neonatal circulatory transition to changes in pulmonary and systemic vascular resistance.
Use anatomy and physiology to explain flow, mixing, pressure, and oxygen-delivery patterns without equating a pattern with a diagnosis.
Map a clinical question to the ABP universal tasks of pathophysiology, epidemiology/risk, diagnosis, or management.
topics: Qp:Qs as a conceptual flow framework
boardDomains: 14 Conditions Affecting Cardiac Function in the Fetus and Newborn
units.casePractice: Create an anatomy-to-physiology map from a de-identified, linked case description; do not calculate patient-specific therapy or dose.
units.assessment: 10-item physiology annotation and a one-page explanation of a hypothetical mixing physiology.

units.title: Cardiac imaging, ECG, and diagnostic-test interpretation
objectives: Select an imaging or rhythm-study question appropriate to echocardiography, ECG, cross-sectional imaging, or catheterization.
Describe image findings with uncertainty and a differential rather than treating a single image as a final diagnosis.
Recognize the limits of non-invasive measurements and the need for expert review.
units.casePractice: Review only in-site figures from the CC BY Frontiers infant left-atrial-appendage-aneurysm report; record modality, view, finding, and remaining uncertainty.
units.assessment: Structured imaging report for a fictional vignette; graded for reasoning and appropriate escalation, not image-recognition speed.

units.title: Fetal, neonatal, and duct-dependent cardiovascular disease
objectives: Differentiate duct-dependent systemic or pulmonary blood-flow concepts from parallel-circulation physiology.
Interpret current CCHD pulse-oximetry screening outcomes as screening—not exclusion of all CHD.
Explain how prenatal diagnosis, delivery planning, and postnatal transition shape multidisciplinary care.
boardDomains: 14 Conditions Affecting Cardiac Function in the Fetus and Newborn
units.casePractice: Use the CDC algorithm in a fictional newborn-screening exercise; document why a screen is not a definitive diagnostic test.
units.assessment: Open-resource neonatal physiology short-answer set and a safety/escalation reflection.

units.title: Septation, shunts, cyanotic congenital lesions, and situs/venous anatomy
objectives: Classify left-to-right, right-to-left, and mixing physiology using anatomy and timing.
Compare ASD, VSD, AVSD, tetralogy-spectrum, DORV, pulmonary atresia, and anomalous venous return at a conceptual level.
Describe heterotaxy/situs and venous anatomy clearly enough to communicate an imaging question.
boardDomains: 12 Systemic and Pulmonary Venous and Situs Abnormalities
units.casePractice: Compare a fictional anatomy diagram with the CC BY congenital-anomaly case report only for terminology; do not copy or reuse its image without attribution.
units.assessment: Anatomy-to-flow table plus five original differential-diagnosis rationales.

units.title: Single-ventricle lesions and Fontan physiology
objectives: Explain staged single-ventricle palliation as a physiologic pathway rather than a single procedure.
Identify the broad surveillance domains relevant to interstage and Fontan care.
Frame failing-Fontan discussion around multidisciplinary reassessment and evidence limits.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional longitudinal timeline to identify points needing specialist review; no procedure selection or patient-specific recommendation.
units.assessment: Concept map and a one-page evidence question using PICO format.

units.title: Valves, outflow tracts, great arteries, and vascular rings
objectives: Localize valvar/outflow obstruction and relate it to ventricular loading conditions.
Distinguish lesions of the great arteries from vascular rings and explain why cross-sectional anatomy may be needed.
Communicate lifetime follow-up questions across pediatric and adult congenital settings.
units.casePractice: Interpret the linked CC BY infant LAAA case’s stated imaging findings in situ, separating reported facts from inferences.
units.assessment: Six-image-free anatomy sketches with verbal captions and a differential list.

units.title: Arrhythmias, inherited rhythm disease, and electrophysiology
objectives: Use a systematic ECG description to distinguish rate, rhythm, intervals, and QRS morphology.
Compare re-entry, automaticity, triggered activity, bradyarrhythmia, and device concepts.
Recognize that risk and management require paediatric electrophysiology context and current guidance.
boardDomains: 16 Genetic Disorders and Syndromes of the Cardiovascular System
18 Preventative Cardiology and Inherited Cardiovascular Diseases
units.casePractice: Label rate/rhythm/intervals on fictional, instructor-created ECG descriptions; do not substitute them for clinical ECG interpretation.
units.assessment: Original rhythm-reasoning quiz and a referral/escalation communication exercise.

units.title: Acquired inflammatory disease and coronary abnormalities
objectives: Differentiate inflammatory, infectious, ischemic, and congenital causes of pediatric coronary concern.
Summarize the diagnostic and longitudinal questions in Kawasaki disease and MIS-C using current sources.
Explain why fever, shock, or elevated biomarkers demand broad differential diagnosis and multidisciplinary care.
boardDomains: 15 Inflammatory and Infectious Acquired Heart Disease
units.casePractice: Use the CC BY Kawasaki case series only in the linked source; state the documented features and compare them with the 2024 AHA statement, without giving treatment instructions.
units.assessment: Evidence table: feature, alternative diagnosis, source, uncertainty, and referral/monitoring question.

units.title: Myocardium, pericardium, heart failure, transplant, and exercise
objectives: Organize a differential for pediatric ventricular dysfunction by myocardial, structural, rhythm, inflammatory, and systemic causes.
Describe broad heart-failure, transplant, exercise, and rehabilitation concepts without converting educational content into a patient plan.
Appraise the age and evidence limits of therapeutic claims.
boardDomains: 11 Disorders of the Myocardium and Pericardium
units.casePractice: Study the CC BY lipodystrophy-associated cardiomyopathy report in situ; annotate evidence of image consent and license before any allowed educational reuse.
units.assessment: Mechanism-based differential and literature-appraisal worksheet.

units.title: Pulmonary vascular disease, cardiac intensive care, and catheterization context
objectives: Relate pulmonary vascular resistance, ventilation, and congenital anatomy to hemodynamic vulnerability.
Identify the roles and limits of ICU, catheterization, surgery, and imaging teams.
Explain post-operative low-output and pulmonary-hypertension concepts at a systems level.
units.casePractice: Create a non-actionable team map identifying what information each specialty needs in a fictional postoperative handoff.
units.assessment: Closed-loop communication rubric and a safety-focused morbidity-and-improvement mini-analysis.

units.title: Genetics, prevention, adult congenital transition, and family-centered care
objectives: Elicit a three-generation cardiovascular family history and identify questions for genetic counseling.
Explain preventive evaluation of symptoms, sports questions, and inherited-risk concerns without issuing individual clearance decisions.
Design a transition-of-care question set for adolescent-to-adult congenital care.
boardDomains: 7 Congenital Heart Disease in the Adolescent and Adult
16 Genetic Disorders and Syndromes of the Cardiovascular System
18 Preventative Cardiology and Inherited Cardiovascular Diseases
units.casePractice: Write a fictional transition handoff using person-first language, uncertainty, and a family-question prompt.
units.assessment: Family-history pedigree exercise and transition-care communication checklist.

units.title: Systems-based practice, scholarship, quality improvement, and ethical evidence use
objectives: Apply basic study-design, bias, diagnostic-test, and quality-improvement concepts to pediatric cardiology literature.
Discuss access, social determinants, neurodevelopment, privacy, and communication as cardiology practice domains.
Distinguish public educational study from supervised clinical competence, procedure credentialing, or board eligibility.
units.casePractice: Audit the license, consent statement, and provenance of one linked CC BY case before citing it; never download/rehost a file whose permissions are unclear.
units.assessment: Mini protocol or QI charter plus a structured critical appraisal.

assignment.title: Independent pediatric cardiology evidence-and-reasoning portfolio
deliverables: 12 unit learning logs, each identifying a relevant ABP domain, a source, one uncertainty, and one escalation/communication question.
Three fictional case reasoning maps (neonatal/CCHD; rhythm; acquired coronary or myocardial) with no management orders, drug/dose, or procedure recommendation.
One critical appraisal or QI charter using public/de-identified material and a license/provenance audit.
A transition-of-care communication template written for a fictional scenario.
assignment.gradingGuide: Suggested formative rubric: source traceability 30%; physiology/anatomy reasoning 25%; uncertainty and safety boundaries 20%; systems/equity/communication 15%; license/provenance practice 10%. Not validated for board prediction or clinical competency.
assignment.submissionBoundary: For self-study only; not submitted to Boston Children’s, ABP, ACGME, a credentialing body, or a patient record.

formative: Unit quizzes using the original questions below
Structured peer or faculty discussion only under the learner’s own institution
assessment.summativePlan: A 60-minute open-source synthesis: fictional vignette, diagnostic reasoning, source table, and safety/communication plan. Passing is not certification, eligibility, a grade from any institution, or a predictor of examination performance.
assessment.clinicalAssessmentBoundary: No observed patient encounters, procedure assessments, case logs, entrustable professional activities, simulation sign-offs, or supervisor evaluations are provided.

studyHours.label: Transparent independent-study plan, not institutional credit or clinical training time
studyHours.calculationNote: The 36.219444 ready-video hours are a deduplicated total of 44 public recordings. Clinical rotations, observerships, reading time, planned clips, and quizzes are not counted as video lectures.

mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Actual named categorical three-year fellowship, not a generic directory category. Its public page states eight fellows each year. The associated public curriculum page describes 24 months of clinical rotations, 12 months of elective/research, month-long boot camp, and a 13-block schedule; it does not publish a complete lecture library or all competency/procedure requirements.

boardNames: American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) — Pediatric Cardiology
medical.boardStatus: Pediatric Cardiology is an ABP pediatric subspecialty with an ABP in-training, initial certification, and maintenance-of-certification content outline. It is not a separate degree conferred by this independent course.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABP (checked 2026-10-07) states that the ordinary route requires three years of full-time, broad-based pediatric cardiology fellowship in an ACGME-accredited U.S. or RCPSC-accredited Canadian program. General ABP criteria also require initial General Pediatrics certification and maintenance to take a subspecialty examination (subject to the stated pending-result circumstance), a valid unrestricted allopathic/osteopathic license in at least one U.S. jurisdiction/territory or Canada, program-director verification of training/competence/professionalism and scholarly activity, and a passing subspecialty certifying exam. For initial certification, ABP also states that required subspecialty training normally must have been completed within the previous seven years; the pediatric subspecialty examinations are offered every other year. Leaves, part-time training, prior credit, and the exceptional preapproved research fast-track/dual-training pathways have ABP-specific rules. This course, viewing videos, completing quizzes, clinical employment, an observership, or research alone does not establish any requirement, board eligibility, certification, license, or procedure privilege. Confirm current rules directly with ABP.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional newborn is screened at 28 hours of age. The right-hand saturation is 96% and foot saturation is 92% on an initial screen and again one hour later. Which statement best describes the screening result?

options.text: It passes because one measurement is at least 95%.
It fails because saturation is below 95% in either extremity on two measures one hour apart.
It passes because the hand-foot difference is less than 5%.
It is diagnostic of a particular congenital heart defect.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC defines a failed screen as <95% in either right hand or foot on two measures separated by one hour. Screening identifies some CCHDs and is not diagnostic of a specific defect.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional febrile child has shock and elevated cardiac enzymes after a recent infection. Which response best reflects current CDC MIS-C guidance?

options.text: Assume MIS-C and omit alternative diagnoses.
Evaluate alternative diagnoses; cardiac involvement makes echocardiography likely during hospitalization.
Treating teams should never involve cardiology.
A single laboratory value establishes long-term prognosis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC advises evaluation for alternatives because clinical features overlap with other conditions and notes that cardiac involvement will likely prompt at least one echocardiogram. Care decisions require a clinical team.

The child cannot have Kawasaki disease because all classic signs are absent.
An online course can choose treatment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AHA 2024 update addresses diagnosis and cardiac imaging in Kawasaki disease; the linked CC BY case series illustrates diagnostic difficulty in young infants. Neither source turns a course exercise into a treatment decision.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional learner wants to use a published pediatric echocardiographic figure in a slide deck. The source is a Frontiers case report marked CC BY and includes guardian consent for publication. What is the best next step?

options.text: Copy the figure without attribution because it is online.
Credit the authors and original publication, follow the CC BY terms, and avoid implying the image is a new or local patient case.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CC BY permits use with attribution subject to its terms. The consent and license in the cited source support lawful attribution, but do not make it the learner’s case or a diagnostic ground truth for an unrelated patient.

title: Pediatric Cardiology Fellowships
prerequisites: For study: prior pediatric residency-level grounding in pediatric history/examination, congenital anatomy/physiology, ECG basics, pharmacology, evidence appraisal, and medical ethics.

For actual ACGME fellowship entry: ACGME states completion of a qualifying pediatrics or combined internal medicine-pediatrics residency is required; the receiving programme verifies prior competence.
For ABP certification: see the ABP eligibility notice in this entry; requirements are not created or met by this course.
Learners without clinical training should use this as conceptual education only and should not apply content to real-patient decisions.
objectives: Map learning activities to all 21 ABP Pediatric Cardiology Content Outline domains and the four ABP universal tasks.
Explain congenital, fetal/neonatal, acquired, vascular, inherited, and longitudinal-care concepts with explicit uncertainty.
Select questions—not independent orders—that common cardiac tests and advanced imaging may address.
Distinguish public institutional programme descriptions, ACGME accreditation standards, ABP eligibility/blueprint documents, guideline hubs, and lecture recordings.
Critically appraise dated evidence, bias/confounding, patient-image licensing, de-identification, and systems/equity issues.
State clearly why independent study does not replace supervised clinical care, fellowship rotations, procedures, licensure, accreditation, or ABP eligibility.

medical.boardEligibilityNotice: As checked 2026-10-07, ABP states that Pediatric Cardiology certification requires three years of full-time, broad-based fellowship in an ACGME-accredited U.S. or RCPSC-accredited Canadian pediatric cardiology programme, programme-director verification of training/competence/scholarly activity, and a passed subspecialty certifying examination. ABP general criteria also require initial General Pediatrics certification (with limited pending-exam circumstance stated by ABP), continuing certification, and a valid unrestricted allopathic and/or osteopathic license in at least one U.S. jurisdiction, territory, or Canada. The ABP is authoritative; rules are subject to change. Self-study, videos, and this course do not satisfy any of these requirements.

Right-to-Left Shunts
Single-Ventricle Lesions
Coronary Artery Abnormalities

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABP outline lists these lesions under Domain 4, Left-to-Right Shunts. This asks blueprint classification, not how to manage any lesion.

practiceQuestions.stem: A healthy-appearing newborn has a right-hand saturation of 96% and foot saturation of 92% on two measurements separated by one hour. Under the CDC algorithm, which interpretation is correct?

options.text: The screen passes because one value is at least 95%.
The screen fails because saturation is below 95% in either extremity on two measures.
The screen passes because neither value is below 90%.
The algorithm establishes a specific congenital diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC lists a failed screen when saturation is below 95% in either the right hand or foot on two measurements separated by one hour. The algorithm detects some CCHDs and does not establish a specific diagnosis.
practiceQuestions.domain: 8 Duct-Dependent Neonatal Heart Disease / 20 Systems-Based Practice

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes a passing pulse-oximetry CCHD screen in the CDC algorithm?

options.text: At least one extremity is 95% or higher, regardless of the difference.
Both right hand and foot are at least 95% and the absolute difference is 3% or less.
Both values exceed 90%.
A normal physical examination alone is sufficient.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC defines a pass as saturation at least 95% in both right hand and foot with an absolute difference no greater than 3%. A pass does not exclude all CCHD.

title: Pediatric Cardiovascular Intensive Care Fellowship
level: Non-ACGME clinical physician fellowship-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Suggested academic baseline: pediatric cardiovascular anatomy/physiology, basic pediatric critical-care concepts, and evidence appraisal.

For observing or applying to an institutional fellowship, follow that institution’s stated prerequisites; for example, CHOP lists board-certified Pediatrics plus eligible/certified PCCM, pediatric cardiology, pediatric anesthesiology or neonatology, while Johns Hopkins All Children’s lists completed ACGME pediatric cardiology or PCCM fellowship.
Independent learners must not perform procedures, prescribe, interpret a live patient study, or make care decisions from this curriculum.
objectives: Explain how PCCC advanced fellowships relate to—but do not create—ABP PCCM or pediatric cardiology certification.
Use segmental anatomy and postoperative physiology to formulate questions about oxygen delivery and deterioration.
Interpret trends in perfusion markers within operative, lesion-specific, and multidisciplinary context.
Organize postoperative instability around loading conditions, contractility, rhythm, residual lesions and noncardiac causes.
Describe specialized support concepts including ECMO/ECPR, VAD, transplant, neuroprotection and recovery with explicit scope limits.
Apply published PCCM/cardiology content domains as a transparent crosswalk, not an invented PCCC board blueprint.
Construct ethical, family-centered handoffs, debriefs and QI questions.

units.title: Scope, teams, and high-reliability CICU practice
objectives: Distinguish PCCC advanced fellowship from ABP-recognized certification pathways.
Frame bedside care as multidisciplinary, family-centered, and escalation-based rather than independent practice.
units.casePractice: Write a closed-loop handoff for a fictional post-bypass infant; identify three uncertainties and the required attending/surgeon escalation.
units.assessment: Observed structured handoff rubric; no clinical privilege is awarded.

units.title: Segmental anatomy and physiology of critical congenital heart disease
objectives: Relate anatomy, shunt direction, pulmonary/systemic flow, and oxygen delivery without using a single saturation as a universal target.
Recognize duct-dependent and cyanotic physiology as time-sensitive patterns requiring specialist pathways.
units.casePractice: Linked-only Radiopaedia HLHS and TOF cases; state anatomy, postoperative context, and questions for the cardiac imaging team.
units.assessment: Anatomy-to-physiology concept map plus short answer.

units.title: Post-cardiopulmonary-bypass physiology and low cardiac output
objectives: Interpret oxygen-delivery markers and trends after surgery while recognizing blood pressure may be a late or incomplete signal.
Build a differential that includes preload/afterload/contractility/rhythm, residual lesion, bleeding, and noncardiac causes.
units.casePractice: Fictional post-bypass deterioration: trend lactate, urine output, perfusion and echo question; rank causes without selecting a drug or dose.
units.assessment: Trend-interpretation worksheet with reassessment triggers.

units.title: Hemodynamic monitoring, ventilation, and pulmonary vascular physiology
objectives: Explain cardiopulmonary interactions and why ventilator changes may alter cardiac loading conditions.
Select questions a monitor, blood gas, imaging study, or echo can answer; name limitations and confounders.
units.casePractice: For a fictional ventilated child with CHD, create a monitor-to-decision table and mark which interpretation needs bedside expert review.
units.assessment: Annotated tracing/monitoring vignette.

units.title: Perioperative lesion pathways and residual-lesion thinking
objectives: Apply a structured postoperative review: operation/expected physiology, observed trajectory, discrepancy, and escalation.
Avoid treating a generic ICU pathway as interchangeable with lesion-specific congenital physiology.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional postoperative pathway card with expected findings and red flags; no prescriptive treatment orders.
units.assessment: Postoperative mismatch differential and escalation rationale.

units.title: Single-ventricle and staged-palliation care
objectives: Explain why Stage 1, Glenn, and Fontan circulations require lesion- and stage-specific reasoning.
Identify interstage surveillance and family communication as systems tasks, not substitutes for urgent review.
units.casePractice: Use the link-only HLHS case to map anatomy to possible stage-specific questions; do not infer management from an image alone.
units.assessment: Stage-to-physiology comparison matrix.

units.title: Rhythm, pacing, and acute postoperative instability
objectives: Relate rate, AV synchrony, filling, and cardiac output in postoperative children.
Recognize that rhythm disturbance with instability requires immediate team-based assessment for mechanical and physiologic contributors.
units.casePractice: Fictional rhythm-strip interpretation: formulate data requests and senior escalation, not a standalone treatment plan.
units.assessment: Rhythm/physiology explanation.

units.title: Resuscitation, arrest prevention, and crisis resource management
objectives: Identify physiologic deterioration patterns and coordinate role allocation, communication, and post-event learning.
Differentiate a general pediatric arrest framework from an individualized congenital-cardiac resuscitation plan.
units.casePractice: Tabletop fictional CICU arrest: designate roles, communication loop, and debrief questions.
units.assessment: Crisis-resource-management checklist.

units.title: Heart failure, transplant, and ventricular assist support
objectives: Differentiate chronic/acute decompensation concepts and recognize when advanced-heart-failure collaboration is needed.
Describe VAD/transplant as specialized program decisions with patient-specific candidacy and ethics, not self-study interventions.
units.casePractice: Fictional trajectory mapping: list worsening markers and the specialties that must co-plan escalation.
units.assessment: Evidence-summary memo with uncertainty statement.

units.title: ECMO, ECPR, and mechanical circulatory support
objectives: Explain broad indications, contraindications, monitoring, and complications of pediatric cardiac ECMO.
Recognize that post-cardiac-surgery ECMO should prompt early investigation of residual lesions and that support strategy is anatomy/center specific.
units.casePractice: Fictional multidisciplinary ECMO huddle: identify candidacy questions, residual-lesion evaluation, and family communication needs; no cannulation instruction.
units.assessment: ECMO indications/limitations concept check.

units.title: Neuroprotection, analgesia/sedation, delirium, and recovery
objectives: Integrate neurodevelopment, analgesia/sedation, delirium screening, and family-centered recovery into perioperative plans.
State why early extubation is a selected-patient strategy rather than a universal target.
units.casePractice: Compare fictional high- and low-complexity postoperative scenarios against the published selected-patient early-extubation caveat.
units.assessment: Recovery-plan critique.

units.title: Multiorgan care: kidney, fluid, hematology, nutrition, infection
objectives: Connect fluid balance, kidney injury, hematology/coagulation, nutrition, and infection risk to cardiac physiology and device support.
Use trends and multidisciplinary consultation rather than isolated laboratory values to judge response.
units.casePractice: Fictional daily goals table: show links among fluid balance, perfusion markers, ventilation and nutrition; identify missing data.
units.assessment: Integrated multiorgan trend note.

units.title: Ethics, communication, quality improvement, and transition to faculty
objectives: Use respectful, family-centered communication and recognize consent/assent, uncertainty, and palliative-care consultation boundaries.
Design a small QI question with process, outcome, and balancing measures appropriate to a CICU.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional family-meeting agenda and a one-page QI charter; neither replaces local ethics/QI oversight.
units.assessment: Faculty-style feedback on communication and QI charter.

assignment.title: Fictional CICU physiology-and-systems portfolio
deliverables: One operation-aware fictional postoperative handoff and trend interpretation.
One single-ventricle or cyanotic-CHD anatomy-to-physiology map using link-only licensed case material.
One ECMO/residual-lesion question map with explicit no-procedure boundary.
One family-meeting agenda and one QI charter with process, outcome and balancing measures.
assignment.guardrails: Use only fictional scenarios or linked public de-identified resources. Do not upload patient records, copy protected images, use proprietary exam material, or give patient-specific treatment advice.

assessment.format: 10 original formative MCQs, 13 unit checks, case-reflection portfolio and QI/communication rubric.
assessment.standard: Pass/fail self-study feedback only; not validated for ABP or other examination performance and not a licensure, credentialing or clinical-competence assessment.
assessment.feedback: Compare reasoning to cited sources and discuss real clinical questions with a qualified supervisor/local protocol.

mapping.name: Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Fellowship / CICU Senior Fellowship Program
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Actual one-year senior fellowship, not a generic directory category. The page states 2–5 fellows/year in a 44-bed medical/surgical cardiac unit; individualized month-by-month study plan, electives for differing precursor paths, weekly one-hour seminar, and 360 evaluation. It does not publish a full lecture catalogue or certify hours.

mapping.name: Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: One-year advanced fellowship. CHOP publishes five-to-six months CICU plus background-tailored rotations: cardiology-trained fellows have PICU/airway/sedation; PCCM/anesthesia/neonatology-trained fellows have echo, catheterization, morphology, HF/transplant and electrophysiology blocks. This is an institutional variant, not an ABP credential.

mapping.name: Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: One-year advanced fellowship. Published rotations include 24 weeks CICU, 2–6 weeks cardiac anesthesia/surgery/perfusion, six weeks research/elective; cardiac echo/catheterization/EP or PICU vary by prior training.

mapping.name: Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: One-year advanced fellowship. Published schedule has 24 CICU weeks, four cardiac anesthesia/surgery/perfusion, six elective, four research, with PICU/airway for prior cardiology and echo/catheterization/EP for prior PCCM. Its listed applicant requirement is completed ACGME pediatric cardiology or PCCM fellowship.

unitMap.text: Scope, teams, and high-reliability CICU practice
Segmental anatomy and physiology of critical congenital heart disease
Post-cardiopulmonary-bypass physiology and low cardiac output
Hemodynamic monitoring, ventilation, and pulmonary vascular physiology
Perioperative lesion pathways and residual-lesion thinking
Single-ventricle and staged-palliation care
Rhythm, pacing, and acute postoperative instability
Resuscitation, arrest prevention, and crisis resource management
Heart failure, transplant, and ventricular assist support
ECMO, ECPR, and mechanical circulatory support
Neuroprotection, analgesia/sedation, delirium, and recovery
Multiorgan care: kidney, fluid, hematology, nutrition, infection
Ethics, communication, quality improvement, and transition to faculty

topicGaps: No public source was found that constitutes a complete, current, institution-endorsed full PCCC lecture series or a PCCC board blueprint.

The ledger has less lesion-specific, operation-specific depth for Norwood/Glenn/Fontan postoperative troubleshooting, temporary pacing details, and cardiac-ECMO decompression than would be taught under supervision.
Recorded lectures vary in date and provider; primary guideline/board sources, not video narration, govern accuracy.
No clinical simulation, procedural observation, patient volume, direct supervision, feedback, or local credentialing is included.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

The two ABP boards named here are adjacent, separately recognized subspecialties—not credentials conferred by this course or by a one-year PCCC fellowship.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent study course confers no eligibility. ABP PCCM and pediatric cardiology certification each require three years of full-time ACGME/RCPSC-accredited fellowship, program verification (including scholarship), applicable ABP criteria and the relevant examination. ABP general criteria also include general pediatrics certification/MOC and an unrestricted U.S./Canada license. Verify current requirements directly with ABP.

officialProgrammes.name: Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Fellowship / CICU Senior Fellowship Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Actual one-year senior fellowship, not a generic directory category. officialProgrammes.name: Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Medicine Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: One-year advanced fellowship. officialProgrammes.name: Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: One-year advanced fellowship. Published rotations include 24 weeks CICU, 2–6 weeks cardiac anesthesia/surgery/perfusion, six weeks research/elective; cardiac echo/catheterization/EP or PICU vary by prior training.

officialProgrammes.name: Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: One-year advanced fellowship. Published schedule has 24 CICU weeks, four cardiac anesthesia/surgery/perfusion, six elective, four research, with PICU/airway for prior cardiology and echo/catheterization/EP for prior PCCM. Its listed applicant requirement is completed ACGME pediatric cardiology or PCCM fellowship.

medical.programmeSourceScope: MED-027 is an actual separate advanced clinical fellowship category, not a generic directory category. Transparent study scope: it synthesizes public PCCC competencies and published institutional rotation descriptions into independent didactic study for advanced clinicians/learners. It does not claim that the sources are one uniform programme, that every listed program has the same prerequisites, or that clinical rotations are lecture hours.
sourceCaveats: Boston Children’s page identifies a clinical fellowship and a weekly one-hour seminar but does not publish a complete lecture set or lecture durations. No clinical rotation is counted as video instruction.
PCICS is a specialty-society directory/consensus source. It supports the non-ACGME pathway boundary but does not confer certification.

ABP outlines are authentic PCCM/cardiology examination blueprints. ABP explicitly cautions that content outlines are not curriculum or study guides; they are used here only as transparent adjacent-domain crosswalks.

The video ledger records public metadata duration and provider identity. It does not validate every statement made in a recording; medical claims should be checked against the cited primary guidelines.
Radiopaedia/MedPix/CAP cases are linked, not copied or rehosted. No real patient record, diagnostic scan, or synthetic patient image is included in these deliverables.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional infant several hours after cardiopulmonary bypass becomes cool and mottled with falling urine output and a rising lactate, while the arterial pressure has changed little. Which interpretation is best?

options.text: Stable blood pressure excludes inadequate oxygen delivery.
The trend supports concern for impaired perfusion/low output and requires urgent contextual reassessment.
Lactate alone identifies a residual lesion.
Only direct cardiac-output measurement can guide any next step.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The PCICS guide lists physical-perfusion findings, urine output, lactate, venous saturation and end-organ function as useful markers; blood pressure may be less reliable and can be late. The pattern is concerning but does not establish one cause.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional post-operative child, marked tachycardia coincides with poorer filling and perfusion. Which mechanism is most directly relevant to the team’s physiologic discussion?

options.text: Tachycardia always increases stroke volume.
Tachycardia can shorten diastolic filling time and increase myocardial oxygen demand.
Heart rate is unrelated to cardiac output in children.
Tachycardia confirms sepsis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The postoperative-care guide notes that tachycardia can compromise ventricular filling, reduce coronary filling time and increase oxygen demand; it is not diagnostic of one etiology.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional child is placed on VA ECMO after cardiac surgery for persistent low output. Which concurrent question is specifically supported by the ELSO pediatric cardiac-failure guideline?

options.text: Whether a residual anatomical lesion requires early investigation and management.
Whether all future imaging should be deferred until decannulation.
Whether ECMO eliminates the need to assess end-organ perfusion.
Whether cannulation strategy is independent of congenital anatomy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ELSO says postoperative cardiac ECMO should prompt early investigation and management of possible residual lesions, and describes anatomy/surgical palliation as relevant to strategy.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes early extubation after pediatric cardiac surgery?

options.text: It is required for every child in an enhanced-recovery pathway.
It is feasible in selected patients; instability, low output, residual lesions, severe pulmonary hypertension and respiratory issues can favor longer ventilation.
It is determined solely by age.
It makes delirium screening unnecessary.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AATS consensus recommends immediate/early extubation as part of enhanced recovery in selected patients and lists risk factors for prolonged invasive ventilation; it also recommends delirium screening.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional child after congenital-heart surgery is agitated and difficult to assess. Which course principle is most defensible?

options.text: Assume agitation is behavioral before assessing physiology.
Use an age-appropriate delirium screen within an integrated assessment of pain, sedation, hemodynamics and neurologic status.
Use a single sedative as a universal first-line answer.
Delay all screening until hospital discharge.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AATS pediatric congenital-heart-surgery consensus recommends age-appropriate ICU delirium screening. It should accompany, not replace, a physiologic assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement accurately describes PCCC fellowship certification status in the United States?

options.text: Completing a one-year PCCC fellowship automatically confers an ABP PCCC certificate.
The ACGME currently accredits a standalone PCCC pathway.
PCCC advanced fellowships are not currently ACGME-accredited; ABP PCCM and pediatric cardiology are separate recognized certification routes with their own required accredited training and exams.
The PCCC fellowship substitutes for general pediatrics certification and licensure.

practiceQuestions.rationale: PCICS states that ACGME does not currently accredit this pathway. ABP separately requires three years of accredited/RCPSC PCCM or cardiology fellowship plus verification and the relevant subspecialty examination.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional cardiology-trained PCCC fellow seeks a curriculum experience that fills general critical-care rather than cardiology knowledge gaps. Which published CHOP rotation most directly reflects that individualized bridge?

options.text: Four weeks of PICU.
Four weeks of catheterization only.
No exposure outside the CICU.
Automatic independent attending coverage.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CHOP lists four weeks of pediatric ICU and airway/sedation experiences for fellows with prior pediatric cardiology training; this is an institutional curriculum description, not a universal requirement.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a fictional postoperative patient with a new rhythm disturbance and impaired perfusion, which is the strongest first reasoning frame?

options.text: Classify the rhythm, then ignore anatomy and ventricular filling.
Assess rate/rhythm and AV synchrony together with filling, loading conditions, operation context and other mechanical causes of deterioration.
Treat every postoperative rhythm disturbance as identical.
Wait for spontaneous resolution before notifying the team.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The PCICS guide links heart rate/rhythm to cardiac output and discusses AV synchrony; post-operative instability requires a broad, anatomy-aware differential.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which item is explicitly represented in the ABP PCCM content outline under organ-support therapies and monitoring?

options.text: Mechanical circulatory support devices including ECMO and ventricular support.
A PCCC-specific certification examination blueprint.
Independent congenital cardiac surgery credentialing.
A required institutional CICU rotation schedule.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The PCCM outline includes mechanical circulatory support devices including ECMO and ventricular support under organ support. It does not create a PCCC certificate or prescribe one institution’s rotations.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional family asks whether a single online course or advanced fellowship year qualifies a clinician to make a high-risk CICU decision alone. What is the appropriate answer?

options.text: Yes, video completion independently grants CICU authority.
Yes, any PCCC fellowship replaces local credentialing.

No; clinical decisions require the licensed, credentialed care team and local supervision. Independent study does not replace supervised training, licensure, institutional privileges or board eligibility.
Only a textbook is needed to decide.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The course is independent study. PCICS describes non-ACGME advanced training, while ABP eligibility requires specific accredited training, licensure and verification; none is conferred here.

title: Pediatric Electrophysiology Fellowship
level: Non-ACGME clinical physician fellowship; independent-study curriculum aligned to its public scope-aligned independent study
prerequisites: MD/DO or comparable clinical training level; completed pediatrics and pediatric cardiology foundations are assumed for advanced material.
Working skill in basic pediatric ECG interpretation, congenital anatomy, acute-care escalation, pharmacology, and evidence appraisal.
For procedural topics, observe only through authorized institutional training and follow local supervision, credentialing, radiation, infection-control, and consent rules.
objectives: Interpret pediatric rhythm information with age, anatomy, clinical context, and uncertainty stated explicitly.
Map study to ABP pediatric-cardiology domains without claiming a pediatric-EP board exam.
Explain principles—not independent performance—of EP study, mapping, ablation, pacing, ICD/CRT, and device follow-up.
Integrate fetal, inherited, CHD, post-operative, and transition considerations into a multidisciplinary reasoning framework.
Critically compare dated recordings with current consensus/guidelines and articulate accreditation, eligibility, and clinical-practice boundaries.

units.title: Supraventricular, junctional, and bradyarrhythmias

units.title: EP study, intracardiac electrograms, pacing maneuvers, and mapping

units.title: Catheter ablation in children and congenital heart disease

units.title: Pacing, ICDs, CRT, and lead stewardship

Relate pediatric growth, CHD anatomy, and lifetime lead management to device discussions.

units.casePractice: Use a fictional device alert narrative to state immediate safety concerns and the appropriate supervised escalation.
units.assessment: Device-troubleshooting concept map; no programming or remote-device instruction.

units.title: Arrhythmias in congenital and post-operative heart disease
objectives: Relate repairs, scars, hemodynamics, and access constraints to rhythm evaluation.

units.casePractice: Fictional post-operative narrative: explain why anatomy and operative history must be reviewed before rhythm attribution.
units.assessment: Multidisciplinary handoff note (de-identified fictional case).

units.title: Sudden-death prevention, exercise, genetics, and communication
objectives: Use a structured approach to syncope/palpitations and family history.

units.casePractice: Fictional family meeting: practice plain-language explanation of a non-diagnostic result and referral rationale.
units.assessment: Patient-family communication OSCE script (educational role play).

units.title: Quality, research, professional boundaries, and longitudinal practice
objectives: Appraise observational EP evidence and recognize bias/limited generalizability.
State the difference between independent study, supervised fellowship, certification, licensure, and device/procedure credentialing.

units.casePractice: De-identify a fictional QI abstract and identify confounding, outcome, and disclosure issues.
units.assessment: Structured critical appraisal plus reflective scope statement.

assignment.title: Evidence-anchored pediatric EP portfolio
components: 10 structured ECG/rhythm interpretation worksheets using authorized link-only or fictional material
One congenital/post-operative arrhythmia handoff using a fictional case
One 750-word critical appraisal of an EP/CIED/ablation source
One patient-family communication script that labels uncertainty and supervised referral
assignment.submissionBoundary: Educational portfolio only. No real patient data, images, recordings, device screenshots, identifiers, or treatment plans may be submitted.

formative: Unit checks and annotated reasoning logs
Feedback against a rubric for safety, age/CHD context, evidence, uncertainty, and professional boundaries
assessment.summativePlan: Original 40-item open-resource knowledge assessment (not included here), portfolio rubric, and oral case-reasoning simulation using a fictional vignette. Passing does not predict any board result.
assessment.prohibitedClaims: No procedural competency sign-off, clinical case-volume credit, CME claim, board-prep guarantee, or certification is awarded.

medical.trackType: Non-ACGME clinical physician fellowship; independent-study curriculum aligned to its public scope
boardNames: American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) – Pediatric Cardiology
International Board of Heart Rhythm Examiners (IBHRE) – voluntary physician certification examinations, not ABMS/ABP specialty certification
medical.boardStatus: No separate ABP/ABMS third-tier certification in pediatric electrophysiology. The ABP certifies Pediatric Cardiology; its content outline is used only as a broad pediatric-cardiology blueprint. The 2015 AHA pediatric-cardiology training statement reports that IBHRE offers certification examinations in pediatric cardiac electrophysiology and cardiac rhythm device therapy; verify current IBHRE eligibility directly before applying.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This self-study does not confer or document ACGME training, ABP eligibility, IBHRE eligibility, licensure, procedure numbers, supervision, institutional privileges, radiation authorization, certification, or a passing outcome. ABP Pediatric Cardiology eligibility requires three years of qualifying broad-based accredited/RCPSC fellowship plus other ABP requirements; a Boston Children’s EP senior fellowship or this course is not stated by ABP to replace that requirement.

officialProgrammes.name: Electrophysiology Senior Fellowship (public page headed Pediatric Electrophysiology)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Actual separate senior clinical fellowship, not merely a directory category. Publicly described as 12–18 months; inpatient acute/chronic arrhythmia service; catheter ablation; CIED implantation; outpatient EP and inherited-arrhythmia management. Individual focus may include exercise testing, adult congenital cardiology, surgical EP, lead stewardship/extraction, and CRT. It expects clinical research/first-author paper and says it satisfies PACES/HRS pediatric EP training guidelines. No public didactic-hour total, complete rotation calendar, case log, accreditation claim, or guarantee of annual funded position is published.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The discovered entry is an actual Boston Children’s EP senior fellowship, not a generic directory CATEGORY. This curriculum transparently studies the public program’s clinical and scholarly scope and national pediatric-EP training recommendations. It does not recreate rotations, assert unpublished experiences, or present other PACES institutions as Boston Children’s variants. PACES reports that pediatric EP is not ACGME-accredited and that programme availability/funding varies; it is an application resource, not a curriculum for this named institution.
sourceCaveats: YouTube durations were observed through public metadata on the stated date and can change if a video is edited/removed/restricted. Publication dates were not consistently available through the metadata probe, so null is retained rather than guessed.
Public recordings are not automatically guidelines, institutionally endorsed curricula, or pediatric-specific. Category labels preserve source identity; general/adult EP content is foundation only.
The PACES ECG module landing page was not ready/free at review. It is neither counted toward video hours nor represented as an available case bank.
Guideline status and device/ablation indications must be checked at point of clinical care. This course has no human clinical review.

title: Vascular Neurology Fellowship

prerequisites.learningLevel: Post-residency/advanced neurology self-study; learners without clinical training may use only conceptually and must not make care decisions.
recommendedKnowledge: basic stroke syndromes and CT/MRI terminology
prerequisites.formalTrainingBoundary: ACGME appointment requires prior neurology, child neurology, or neurodevelopmental-disabilities training. ABPN adds its certification conditions. Neither is met here.

objectives: Localize cerebrovascular syndromes with transparent uncertainty.
Explain current guideline pathways without prescribing care.
Link evaluation/prevention to mechanism.
Interpret imaging questions and limits.
Recognize CVT and uncommon vascular differentials.
Integrate recovery, systems, ethics, and quality improvement.
Map study to public ABPN specifications while preserving boundaries.

units.title: Neurovascular localization, syndromes, and first assessment
objectives: Localize common anterior/posterior circulation syndromes and distinguish key mimics.
Use NIHSS as a structured severity measure without replacing a full examination.
Explain why last-known-well, disability, and territory drive urgency.
units.casePractice: Use linked ISLES MRI data only to compare research lesion-mask location with a supplied label; do not make a patient diagnosis.
units.assessment: 10-item localization/mimic quiz plus a fictional NIHSS rationale.

units.title: Acute ischemic stroke: imaging, triage, and reperfusion reasoning
objectives: Construct a time-critical NCCT-to-vascular/advanced-imaging pathway.
Compare IV thrombolysis and EVT selection logic without independently prescribing.
Explain local systems, LVO identification, and avoidable-imaging-delay issues.
units.casePractice: Use CPAISD anonymized CT research images and labels only for observation; do not infer treatment eligibility.
units.assessment: One-page fictional stroke-code handoff citing the 2026 guideline.

units.title: Mechanism-based ischemic stroke evaluation
objectives: Build a differential across large artery, cardioembolic, small-vessel, dissection, and unusual causes.
Link pattern and imaging to focused etiologic evaluation.
Explain uncertainty around cryptogenic labels.
units.casePractice: Describe location in ISLES legacy data with supplied mask, but do not assign mechanism without clinical data.
units.assessment: Four fictional mechanism matrices with discriminating tests and uncertainty.

units.title: Secondary prevention and cerebrovascular risk
objectives: Match prevention reasoning to established mechanism and context in fictional cases.
Differentiate acute care from long-term prevention.
Explain limits of combination therapy and selected short-term DAPT use.
units.casePractice: Create a non-prescriptive fictional discharge education checklist.
units.assessment: Cited mechanism-specific prevention plan and 12-question quiz.

units.title: Intracerebral and subarachnoid hemorrhage
objectives: Differentiate major ICH causes and high-risk changes.
Explain context-dependent ICH BP guidance.
Describe aSAH transfer, source evaluation, and DCI surveillance.
units.casePractice: Text-only fictional ICH/aSAH vignettes; no generated or purported real patient scan.
units.assessment: ICH/aSAH priority comparison and evidence quiz.

units.title: Cerebral venous thrombosis and uncommon vascular disorders
objectives: Recognize CVT presentations and imaging pathways.
Describe MRI/MRV and CT/CTV roles and escalation context.
Organize differential for dissection, RCVS, moyamoya, and vasculopathy.
units.casePractice: Use CVT guideline figures only at source; do not rehost. Do a fictional headache/seizure imaging-choice exercise.
units.assessment: Short-answer CVT pathway and differential.

units.title: Vascular imaging, ultrasound, and evidence interpretation
objectives: State each modality’s clinical question and limits.
Identify perfusion/vascular-imaging pitfalls.
Appraise guideline, trial, and local-capability interactions.
units.casePractice: Compare CPAISD research labels to observations and list what cannot be concluded.
units.assessment: Modality critique plus 5-minute fictional transfer explanation.

units.title: Neurocritical care, recovery, and rehabilitation
objectives: Identify complications and multidisciplinary recovery needs.
Place rehabilitation and prevention in the continuum.
Use function-focused communication and transition planning.
units.casePractice: Analyze a fictional rehabilitation handoff.
units.assessment: Recovery-plan reflection and team-handoff rubric.

units.title: Stroke systems, quality, ethics, and scholarship
objectives: Map dispatch-to-community stroke systems.
Apply consent, bias, quality, and literature-appraisal principles.
Separate fellowship assessment from independent study.
units.casePractice: Use ASA simulation resources for a fictional local process map only; no credentialed sign-off.
units.assessment: QI storyboard for a hypothetical imaging delay.

units.title: Synthesis: case reasoning and blueprint review
objectives: Integrate localization, imaging, mechanism, acute priorities, and prevention in fictional scenarios.
Map gaps to public ABPN specifications without using proprietary material.
Communicate uncertainty and referral thresholds.
units.casePractice: Three fictional capstones with known/unknown/supervised-decision table.
units.assessment: Open-resource capstone and self-audit; not an ABPN simulation.

assignment.title: Fictional neurovascular case portfolio
deliverables: Three fictional analyses: anterior AIS, ICH/aSAH, CVT or unusual vasculopathy.
For each: syndrome, known/unknown, imaging question, differential, guideline, prevention/recovery or escalation, and supervised-judgment boundary.
300-word critique of a guideline statement versus an older public lecture claim.
assignment.submissionBoundary: No real records, images, identifiers, protected items, or treatment orders.

nonClaims: No grade validates clinical competence, programme completion, or ABPN readiness.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best matches ABPN initial Vascular Neurology certification training requirements outside the expired 2005–2009 practice pathway?

options.text: A rotation during neurology residency is sufficient.
One year of ACGME-accredited vascular-neurology fellowship after neurology or child-neurology residency is required.
Any two-year international stroke fellowship is accepted.
Independent online study substitutes for fellowship.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABPN requires one year of ACGME-accredited fellowship that began after residency; resident exposure does not count and international training is not accepted.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which ABPN competency mechanism has the largest published examination range?

options.text: Mechanism of disease (8–12%)
Diagnostic procedures (22–28%)
Treatment/management (31–39%)
Systems-based practice (1–3%)

practiceQuestions.rationale: The public blueprint lists treatment/management at 31–39%. This is blueprint information, not secure exam content or a score prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult has disabling suspected AIS in the standard early window. Which statement reflects the January 2026 AHA/ASA summary?

options.text: Advanced imaging is always required before eligible IV thrombolysis.
Either alteplase or tenecteplase is endorsed in the 4.5-hour window, with rapid treatment emphasized for eligible disabling deficits.
NIHSS alone determines eligibility regardless of disability.
Adjuvant antithrombotics are recommended with IV thrombolysis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2026 summary endorses either agent in the early window and rapid treatment for eligible disabling deficits; it does not require advanced imaging for standard-window IVT selection and does not recommend adjuvant antithrombotics to enhance IVT. Actual eligibility requires supervised protocol-specific judgment.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the NIH Stroke Scale’s role in this course?

options.text: It replaces a complete neurologic examination.
It is a structured provider tool to assess neurologic function and deficits.
It independently diagnoses vessel occlusion.
Course completion certifies clinical use.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NINDS describes the NIHSS as a provider checklist measuring neurologic function and deficits. It does not replace full assessment or confer authorization through this course.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has mild-to-moderate spontaneous ICH and presenting SBP 180 mm Hg. Which statement reflects the 2022 guideline synopsis?

options.text: A smooth 130–140 mm Hg target range may be reasonable; acute lowering below 130 should be avoided in the stated context.
BP management is never appropriate.
All patients should be abruptly lowered below 110 mm Hg.
A video alone determines BP treatment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline says 130–140 mm Hg is safe and may be reasonable for mild-to-moderate ICH with presenting SBP 150–220, and below 130 is potentially harmful. Educational only; not an order.

practiceQuestions.stem: In fictional aSAH, a new focal deficit develops on day 7. Which framing is most consistent with the 2023 guideline?

options.text: DCI is impossible after aneurysm securing.
DCI commonly occurs days 4–14; expert assessment and TCD, CTA, or CTP can assist in appropriate settings.
Routine hypervolemia is required for every patient.
No monitoring is needed after the first CT.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline describes DCI mostly on days 4–14 and discusses trained assessment plus TCD, CTA, and CTP. It emphasizes euvolemia and avoiding morbidity from hypervolemia.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional young adult has headache and seizure; CVT is a concern. What is best supported by the 2024 AHA statement?

options.text: Only catheter angiography can confirm CVT.
MRI/MRV or CT/CTV are principal diagnostic imaging approaches.
Hemorrhage excludes CVT.
A public dataset image alone diagnoses CVT.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The statement says diagnosis is based primarily on MRI/MRV or CT/CTV and notes diverse presentations including headache and seizures.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which secondary-prevention statement is most faithful to the 2021 AHA/ASA guideline?

options.text: Long-term DAPT is recommended for all survivors.
Antiplatelet plus anticoagulation is generally the default.
Etiologic work-up targets prevention; long-term DAPT is not recommended and short-term DAPT is limited to specific settings.
Mechanism no longer matters after stroke.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline emphasizes etiologic work-up and mechanism-specific prevention, rejects routine long-term DAPT, and limits short-term DAPT to selected settings.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a fictional clinically stable patient with severe symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis, what first-line concept is supported by the cited AAN advisory?

options.text: Routine intracranial stenting first.
Aggressive medical risk-factor management; PTAS is not supported as initial therapy.
No antithrombotic or lipid management.
Choose intervention from a perfusion color map alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The advisory favors intensive medical management and reports no benefit plus higher periprocedural risk for PTAS in studied groups. Individual decisions require specialist care.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which ACGME-required element is not reproduced by this course?

options.text: A monthly teaching conference only.
Progressively responsible, directly supervised clinical assignments and patient-care experience.
Reading an open guideline.
Watching public recordings.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME requires a 12-month program with progressive responsibility, direct supervision, and specified clinical/didactic experiences. This course offers none.

title: Dermatology Residency Program
prerequisites: Physician-level foundational knowledge of anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pharmacology, and clinical history/examination is assumed.
For the referenced ABD pathway, formal prerequisites are regulated PGY-1 and accredited residency training—not self-study.
Learners must not perform biopsies, pathology interpretation, phototherapy, laser/cosmetic procedures, prescribing, or patient-specific management based on this course.
Use linked cases only under their stated licenses; no real patient upload, private health information, or AI training on case images.
objectives: Describe dermatologic morphology and distribution before naming a diagnosis.
Build transparent differentials and recognize when testing, pathology, referral, or urgent evaluation is needed.
Apply current source hierarchy to common medical, pediatric, surgical, and dermatopathology topics.
Distinguish current guideline statements from older public lectures and date-check time-sensitive content.
Use authentic linked case images lawfully and document image provenance, attribution, and diagnostic limits.
Explain ABD pathway boundaries without representing independent study as eligibility or certification.
Correlate clinical patterns with dermatopathology reaction-pattern vocabulary.
Communicate uncertainty, safety-netting, equity, and professional boundaries in fictional educational cases.

units.title: Morphology, skin examination, and diagnostic reasoning

units.title: Eczematous disease, contact dermatitis, and itch

units.title: Papulosquamous, psoriatic, and lichenoid disorders

units.title: Acne, rosacea, hair, and nail disorders

units.title: Cutaneous infections and infestations
objectives: Organize fungal and bacterial skin disease differentials by morphology, site, exposures, and host factors.

units.casePractice: Linked case comparison: record lesion morphology and avoid treating a web image as patient-specific proof.

units.title: Drug eruptions, blistering disorders, and urgent mucocutaneous presentations
objectives: Recognize pattern families of drug eruptions and blistering disease and state the limits of remote diagnosis.

units.casePractice: Use only authentic linked cases; label all conclusions as differential hypotheses and identify an urgent-red-flag pathway.

units.assessment: Reasoned referral/escalation plan for a fictional scenario.

units.title: Pigment, dyspigmentation, and equitable visual diagnosis
objectives: Describe pigmentary change neutrally across a range of skin tones.
Identify limits of image datasets and avoid claiming an image alone establishes a diagnosis.
units.casePractice: Audit image provenance, license, and skin-tone representation before using a linked image in study notes.
units.assessment: Image-source and uncertainty audit.

Map melanoma biopsy/staging concepts and prevention counseling principles to current primary sources.

units.title: Therapeutics, photobiology, procedures, and cosmetic boundaries
objectives: Compare broad therapeutic modalities, monitoring concepts, and contraindication questions using primary guidance.
State why viewing a procedure video cannot authorize procedures, laser use, cosmetics practice, or phototherapy administration.

objectives: Use reaction-pattern language to organize a pathology differential.
Correlate clinical morphology, biopsy context, and histopathology without overcalling a single slide/image.
units.casePractice: Review the linked videos with a pattern log. Video chapter titles are not a complete topic inventory; verify contemporary management in current sources.
units.assessment: 20-pattern terminology quiz plus a clinicopathologic correlation note.

objectives: Frame inpatient/urgent dermatology questions with triage, communication, and uncertainty.
Separate public educational information from supervised patient care and keep guidelines/date checks current.

topicGaps: No verified dedicated public pediatric-dermatology lecture block in the counted sequence.
No verified dedicated supervised procedural/laser/Mohs/inpatient-rotation lecture block; this course does not simulate hands-on training.
The MUSC recordings are 2015–2017 and generic chapter titles do not establish exact content; they cannot serve as current therapeutic guidance.
The ledger has limited explicit skin-of-colour/health-equity and image-provenance teaching.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.boardStatus: ABD is the named initial-certification reference. This course maps only to publicly described ABD BASIC/CORE/APPLIED domains; it is not an ABD course, assessment, eligibility determination, or certification pathway.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: No independent-study activity confers board eligibility. ABD describes 12 months of qualifying PGY-1 clinical training and three years of full-time ACGME-accredited U.S. (or RCPSC-accredited Canadian) dermatology residency training; its APPLIED requirements include an accredited residency, all four CORE modules, program-director final evaluation, and applicable medical-licensure requirements. ABD alone decides individual eligibility. The APPLIED window is annual in the first five years after training, maximum five attempts, subject to ABD policy/deferrals.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult with atopic dermatitis asks whether routine systemic corticosteroids are the preferred long-term systemic strategy. Which statement best matches the current AAD guideline summary?

options.text: They are strongly recommended for long-term control.
They are recommended against; treatment decisions require guideline-based alternatives and clinical context.
They are interchangeable with moisturizers.
They are recommended only because topical therapy exists.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AAD atopic dermatitis page recommends against systemic corticosteroids while describing other systemic/phototherapy recommendations. This is an evidence-recall item, not treatment for a real person.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional acne plan includes an oral antibiotic. Which accompanying principle is specifically highlighted by AAD?

options.text: Use the oral antibiotic indefinitely as monotherapy.
Combine systemic antibiotics with benzoyl peroxide and other topical therapies, and limit systemic antibiotic use.
Avoid all topical therapy.
Use light therapy as a required co-treatment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AAD highlights limiting systemic antibiotics and combining them with benzoyl peroxide and other topical therapies.
