title: Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism Fellowship
prerequisites: Prior foundational knowledge equivalent to internal-medicine endocrine physiology, clinical epidemiology, and safe medication terminology.
Ability to read professional guidelines and appraise publication dates/versions.
For clinical application: participation in an appropriately supervised, accredited clinical environment; this course itself supplies no patient-care authority.
No prerequisite payment, enrollment, protected download, real patient record, or proprietary examination material.
objectives: Use hormone-axis physiology and differential reasoning across adrenal, pituitary, thyroid, diabetes, bone, reproductive and metabolic disorders.
Interpret the published ABIM blueprint as a study map while respecting its limits.
Distinguish screening, confirmation, localization, and supervised procedures.
Use current guideline pages to date-check older recordings.
Critically describe official Johns Hopkins fellowship structure without representing it as course completion.
Recognize emergency/red-flag boundaries and escalate real clinical concerns to qualified care.
Use authentic de-identified cases only through their source links and attribution terms.
State the limits of independent study regarding accreditation, certification, competence, licensure, and clinical decisions.

units.title: Fellowship orientation, endocrine physiology, and evidence appraisal
objectives: Relate hypothalamic-pituitary-target-axis feedback to a diagnostic differential.
Distinguish a programme curriculum, ACGME requirements, ABIM examination blueprint, and a guideline.
Identify when a test result may be altered by assay, medication, physiology, or pre-test conditions.
boardDomains: Cross-cutting reasoning; ABIM assesses diagnostic reasoning and clinical judgment across all categories.
units.casePractice: Construct a one-page axis map for a fictional abnormal-result vignette; do not use patient records.
units.assessment: 10-item evidence-source and physiology check.

units.title: Diabetes mellitus, hypoglycemia, technology, and inpatient reasoning
objectives: Classify common diabetes presentations and hypoglycemia mechanisms.
Interpret CGM/monitoring concepts as an educational tracing exercise.
Map diabetes complications and comorbidities to a longitudinal review plan without prescribing.
topics: Type 1, type 2, other diabetes, and prediabetes
CGM, pumps, inpatient diabetes, pregnancy, microvascular and macrovascular complications
boardDomains: Diabetes Mellitus and Hypoglycemia—24% of typical ABIM CERT examination.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional CGM-pattern worksheet to state what extra history, timing, and medication information would be needed before any interpretation.
units.assessment: Timed single-best-answer set plus a de-identified/training-only CGM tracing annotation.

units.title: Adrenal disorders and endocrine emergencies
objectives: Organize differential diagnoses for adrenal insufficiency, cortisol excess, primary aldosteronism, incidentaloma, catecholamine excess, CAH, and adrenal malignancy.
Explain why primary aldosteronism screening uses aldosterone and renin with context-aware interpretation.
Recognize that suspected adrenal crisis is an emergency requiring clinical escalation, not home self-management.
topics: Primary aldosteronism, adrenal venous sampling concepts
boardDomains: Adrenal Disorders—10%; includes glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids, CAH, incidentaloma and pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma.
units.casePractice: Link-only review of the Radiopaedia adrenal-adenoma case; identify imaging clues versus the separate question of hormonal function.
units.assessment: Algorithm critique: list pre-analytic/medication factors that can confound aldosterone-renin interpretation.

units.title: Pituitary, hypothalamic, and water-balance disorders
objectives: Localize pituitary/hypothalamic dysfunction using axis-based reasoning.
Compare common mechanisms of polyuria/polydipsia and hyponatremia conceptually.
Describe when visual symptoms and imaging findings warrant urgent supervised evaluation.
topics: Prolactin, GH, ACTH, TSH and gonadotropin disorders
boardDomains: Pituitary Disorders—10%; the blueprint names MRI phenotypes and inferior petrosal sinus sampling.
units.casePractice: Link-only hidden-diagnosis review of the published Radiopaedia pituitary macroadenoma case; identify the optic-chiasm concern and state that it needs supervised care.
units.assessment: Structured localization table and 8-question image/axis quiz.

units.title: Integrated endocrine testing, imaging, procedures, and safety boundaries
objectives: State the limits of a screening test, confirmatory test, localization study, and procedure.
Describe—without attempting—thyroid ultrasound, thyroid aspiration biopsy, DXA interpretation, and adrenal venous sampling as supervised competencies.
Apply radiation, contrast, pregnancy, and incidental-finding safety questions to an escalation checklist.
topics: Thyroid US/FNA, DXA, AVS, procedure supervision
boardDomains: Cross-cutting; ABIM policy names thyroid FNA, thyroid ultrasound, DXA interpretation, pumps, and CGM as fellowship procedure requirements.
units.casePractice: For an invented scenario, classify each next step as information-gathering, specialist procedure, or not justified from supplied data.
units.assessment: Safety/indication checklist; no simulated or real procedure is performed.

units.title: Female reproduction, PCOS, and endocrine issues across life stages
objectives: Build a differential for amenorrhea and hyperandrogenism while accounting for pregnancy, medications, and non-PCOS causes.
Apply the 2023 international PCOS diagnostic framing at a conceptual level.
Recognize special diagnostic limits in adolescence and the need to exclude alternate etiologies.
units.casePractice: Fictional irregular-menses vignette: specify required history, pregnancy consideration, biochemical assessment quality, and alternative causes—no diagnosis is rendered.
units.assessment: Single-best-answer questions plus a differential matrix.

units.title: Male reproduction, prolactin, and androgen disorders
objectives: Differentiate primary from secondary hypogonadism with physiology-based test selection.
Frame hyperprolactinemia as a differential that includes medications and pituitary disease.
Recognize infertility and gender-related care as multidisciplinary, patient-centered domains requiring current expert guidance.
units.casePractice: Fictional low-testosterone vignette: write a sequence of confirmatory/context questions, not a therapy order.
units.assessment: Interpretation mini-OSCE on a fictional lab panel.

units.title: Calcium, parathyroid, metabolic bone, and osteoporosis
objectives: Differentiate PTH-mediated from non-PTH-mediated hypercalcemia conceptually.
Interpret bone-density terminology and fracture-risk context without substituting for clinical care.
Compare primary, secondary, and tertiary hyperparathyroidism and recognize complex metabolic bone disease referrals.
topics: Osteoporosis, osteomalacia, rickets, vitamin D, hypophosphatemia
Renal osteodystrophy, nephrolithiasis, Paget disease, rare bone disorders
units.casePractice: Link-only blinded review of the Radiopaedia parathyroid adenoma case; distinguish localization imaging from the biochemical diagnosis.
units.assessment: Bone/calcium physiology map, DXA-report terminology exercise, and 12 SBA items.

units.title: Metabolic disease, obesity, nutrition, and lipid disorders
objectives: Organize primary and secondary causes of dyslipidemia and hypertriglyceridemia.
Discuss obesity as a chronic disease with comorbidities and evidence appraisal, not moral judgment.
Identify nutrition and medication questions that require individualized supervised care.
units.casePractice: Fictional lipid panel: list secondary-cause history and laboratory checks before labeling a primary disorder.
units.assessment: Evidence table comparing mechanisms, comorbidities, and uncertainty.

units.title: Thyroid function, nodules, cancer, and pregnancy-aware care
objectives: Interpret thyroid-function patterns with medication, illness, pregnancy, and assay-interference context.
Differentiate evaluation pathways for hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, nodules, and thyroid cancer.
Use the ATA guideline index to identify the most current condition-specific document rather than relying on an old recording.
topics: Differentiated, medullary, anaplastic thyroid cancer; pregnancy
units.casePractice: Fictional thyroid-test discordance: identify possible non-thyroidal illness, medications, and assay interference before a conclusion.
units.assessment: Thyroid-function pattern set and guideline-version audit.

units.title: Consultation, longitudinal care, scholarship, and systems practice
objectives: Present a concise endocrine consult question and uncertainty statement.
Explain how continuity care, technology, social determinants, and team roles influence safe endocrine care.
Critically appraise a guideline update and write a transparent learning reflection.
topics: Research ethics, quality improvement, health equity
boardDomains: Cross-cutting ABIM tasks: diagnosis, test interpretation, treatment recommendation, prognosis/risk, and pathophysiology.
units.casePractice: Submit an invented consult note with problem representation, evidence source, and red-flag escalation line.
units.assessment: Portfolio review and peer feedback rubric; no real patient notes.

units.title: Board-blueprint synthesis and safe independent-study capstone
objectives: Allocate study time using the ABIM blueprint percentages without treating them as a guarantee of test content.
Integrate endocrine axes in complex fictional cases.
State clearly what independent study cannot confer: clinical competence sign-off, board eligibility, licensure, or credentialing.
boardDomains: All eight ABIM content categories; diabetes 24%, calcium/bone 15%, thyroid 15%, lipids/obesity/nutrition 12%, adrenal 10%, pituitary 10%, female reproduction 7%, male reproduction 7%.
units.casePractice: Capstone: two original fictional cases with cited rationale and a separate limitations statement.
units.assessment: 60-question original formative exam, blueprint tag audit, and reflective gap plan.

assignment.title: Source-annotated fictional endocrine consult portfolio
deliverables: Two original fictional problem representations from different blueprint categories.
For each: differential, missing data, red flags/escalation statement, a current guideline/source version, and a 250-word uncertainty reflection.
One one-page ABIM-blueprint study allocation explaining why category percentages guide—not guarantee—coverage.
No real patient data, copied commercial question stems, treatment orders, dose calculations, or diagnostic-image rehosting.
assignment.passingNote: Formative feedback only; no clinical-competence, board, or credentialing determination.

formative: Fictional case differentials and image-link observation logs
Peer discussion of uncertainty and social-context questions
assessment.summativePlan: Original 60-item single-best-answer formative assessment tagged to blueprint categories plus portfolio rubric. Items are not ABIM questions, not validated for passing prediction, and not a substitute for clinical assessment.
assessment.integrity: No proprietary ESAP/board content, no protected downloads, no real patient records, and no claim of score equivalence.

topicGaps: No ready-hour gap exists, but many recordings predate current guidelines; current management must be checked against the listed official sources.

The public video set has limited direct evidence of current inpatient diabetes workflows, diabetes technology interpretation, gender-related endocrine care, assay interference, pregnancy-specific endocrinology, and longitudinal health-equity teaching.
There is no public, complete Johns Hopkins lecture archive confirmed by this research. Johns Hopkins rotations, conferences, and didactics are not counted as external video.
No video, fictional case, or plan can verify procedural competence in FNA, ultrasound, DXA interpretation, pumps/CGM, or adrenal venous sampling.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Endocrinology, Diabetes, and Metabolism Certification Examination
medical.boardStatus: ABIM offers a separate Endocrinology, Diabetes, and Metabolism subspecialty certification examination. The January 2026 ABIM CERT blueprint is the board-content source used here; it is not an official curriculum or question bank.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABIM states that at application a physician must already be ABIM-certified in internal medicine; complete requisite ACGME/RCPSC/Collège des médecins du Québec accredited fellowship training; demonstrate clinical competence/procedural skills/professional behavior; hold a valid unrestricted unchallenged medical license; and pass the examination. For fellows beginning in or after AY 2016–17, ABIM lists a 24-month minimum with 12 clinical months and specified competencies/procedures including thyroid aspiration biopsy, thyroid ultrasound, DXA interpretation, insulin-pump management, and CGM. Only an accredited programme and its ABIM-certified programme director can verify competence. This self-study course creates none of those conditions and grants no eligibility, certification, license, privileges, or guarantee of passing.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This is an actual, separately named Johns Hopkins clinical physician fellowship—not a generic directory category. Transparent study scope: adult endocrinology, diabetes and metabolism knowledge and reasoning aligned to the published ABIM blueprint. It excludes the separately named Johns Hopkins Pediatric Endocrinology fellowship, endocrine surgery, reproductive endocrinology/infertility fellowship, and research-only posts. The supplied nuclear-medicine/radiology outline is unrelated to this item and is not imported. This course is independently authored from public sources and is unaffiliated with Johns Hopkins, ACGME, ABIM, ADA, or any video provider.
sourceCaveats: Fetched source pages and public YouTube metadata were checked on 2026-10-07. Websites, guideline versions, availability, eligibility policies, and video accessibility can change.
Video duration is observed platform metadata, not a claim that every minute is clinically current or suitable for a particular learner. No video was counted twice.
Recordings are from named providers/channels and are not represented as Johns Hopkins, ABIM, ACGME, or ADA content unless their provider/title says so.
The Johns Hopkins public page says most grand rounds are recorded for fellows, but this does not establish a public archive; those institutional sessions were not counted.
Current guidelines supersede historical recordings where they differ. The source list identifies dates; learners must use local protocols and supervision for real care.

practiceQuestions.stem: According to the January 2026 ABIM CERT blueprint, which category carries the largest typical examination share?

options.text: Adrenal disorders
Diabetes mellitus and hypoglycemia
Calcium and bone disorders
Thyroid disorders

practiceQuestions.rationale: The published blueprint assigns Diabetes Mellitus and Hypoglycemia 24%, larger than every other named category. This is a blueprint fact, not a prediction of any individual examination.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with hypertension is being considered for primary-aldosteronism screening. Which initial testing concept best matches the 2025 Endocrine Society guideline?

options.text: Serum potassium alone establishes the screen
Measure aldosterone and renin and determine an aldosterone-to-renin ratio; obtain potassium to aid interpretation
CT alone identifies all surgically curable disease
A suppressed TSH is the screening test

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline describes screening with serum/plasma aldosterone plus plasma renin and ARR; potassium aids interpretation because hypokalemia can lower aldosterone. Imaging and procedural decisions occur later and depend on context.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional person with a positive primary-aldosteronism screen who is considering surgery, what is the guideline-supported purpose of CT plus adrenal venous sampling (AVS)?

options.text: To prove diabetes type
To reliably distinguish lateralizing from bilateral aldosterone excess when deciding a surgical approach
To replace all biochemical testing
To evaluate thyroid cytology

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2025 guideline suggests CT plus AVS before surgery to distinguish lateralizing from bilateral forms, with a narrow exception described by the guideline. This question tests purpose, not procedural performance.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional acutely ill person has severe symptoms concerning for adrenal crisis. Which learning statement best reflects the Endocrine Society primary-adrenal-insufficiency resource?

options.text: Wait for all confirmatory tests before treatment
Immediate medication treatment is indicated while diagnostic results are pending; confirmatory testing can follow when the condition allows
Self-treat at home without evaluation
A bone-density scan confirms the diagnosis

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline resource states that severe symptoms or adrenal crisis should receive immediate treatment until test results are available and that corticotropin stimulation confirms diagnosis when the condition allows. Real emergencies require urgent clinical care.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult fictional vignette has ovulatory dysfunction and clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism after appropriate exclusion of alternate causes. Under the 2023 international PCOS guideline summary, which additional test is necessarily required to establish PCOS?

options.text: Ultrasound or AMH is always required
Neither ultrasound nor AMH is required when those two features are present in adults
Adrenal venous sampling
Pituitary surgery

practiceQuestions.rationale: The source states that in adults, when irregular cycles/ovulatory dysfunction and hyperandrogenism are present, ultrasound or AMH are not required after excluding other etiologies. It also makes different cautionary statements for adolescents.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has high calcium and high PTH, and localization imaging shows a lesion adjacent to the thyroid. What is the most accurate interpretation for a study exercise?

options.text: The image alone establishes the biochemical diagnosis
Biochemistry and clinical context establish the endocrine disorder; imaging contributes localization information
The image proves osteoporosis severity
The image rules out all multigland disease

practiceQuestions.rationale: The linked published parathyroid case provides a concrete localization example with high PTH/calcium, but an image is not a substitute for biochemical and clinical evaluation. This distinction is central to safe endocrine reasoning.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which content area is explicitly listed in the ABIM endocrine blueprint under thyroid disorders?

options.text: Thyroid cancer
Pulmonary embolism
Coronary angiography
Inflammatory bowel disease

practiceQuestions.rationale: The blueprint lists hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, nodules/goiter, thyroid cancer, test abnormalities, and thyroid disease in pregnancy.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional 75-year-old has headache, visual disturbance, and a large sellar mass compressing the optic chiasm on an educational case. Which is the safest learning conclusion?

options.text: It can be managed solely by watching lectures
Mass effect/visual symptoms are a red flag for urgent supervised clinical assessment; image review is not independent management
No endocrine evaluation is relevant
The case can be used as a real patient record

practiceQuestions.rationale: The linked Radiopaedia case describes visual disturbance and chiasmal compression. The course uses it only as a de-identified, linked image-learning resource; real symptoms require supervised clinical evaluation.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which item is an ABIM certification training/procedure requirement for fellows beginning in or after academic year 2016–17, rather than a competency that independent study can sign off?

options.text: Management of insulin pumps
Watching an online lecture
Completing an unaffiliated quiz
Reading a guideline at home

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM lists management of insulin pumps, CGM, thyroid ultrasound, thyroid aspiration biopsy, and skeletal dual-photon absorptiometry interpretation among specified requirements. Eligibility also requires accredited training and program-director competency verification.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes this independent course in relation to the Johns Hopkins fellowship?

options.text: It is an accredited Johns Hopkins clinical rotation
It is a self-study curriculum inspired by public sources and does not replace the two-year supervised fellowship
It grants ABIM eligibility after 36 video hours
It permits supervised procedures without a programme

practiceQuestions.rationale: Johns Hopkins describes a 2-year ACGME fellowship with inpatient and ambulatory training, while ABIM/ACGME require accredited, supervised education and competence. This unaffiliated course provides neither.

title: Gastroenterology Fellowship Program
prerequisites: MD/DO-level foundational medical knowledge or equivalent advanced health-professions study is assumed for the clinical language used here.
Completion of a supervised internal-medicine residency is an ACGME/ABIM training prerequisite for a real GI fellowship; self-study does not meet it.

mapping.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / The Johns Hopkins Hospital
mapping.name: Gastroenterology Fellowship Program
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: This is an actual separate ACGME-accredited programme, not a generic directory category. The current programme curriculum page is https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/gastroenterology-hepatology/education-training/gastroenterology-fellowship. Johns Hopkins describes a clinical three-year track and a research three-year track; both share year-one inpatient GI consults at The Johns Hopkins Hospital and Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center, inpatient endoscopy, and inpatient hepatology. The clinical track’s later years include limited inpatient rotations, outpatient endoscopy, continuity and subspecialty clinics, clinical research and mentoring. The research track limits years two/three to four weeks of inpatient rotations, with protected research time plus one half-day each of outpatient endoscopy, subspecialty and continuity clinic. The directory record separately lists 3-year clinical-scholar/physician-scientist and 4-year clinical-investigator durations; the current curriculum page does not map that 4-year label to either of its two stated 3-year tracks, so the discrepancy is preserved rather than resolved by inference. The page also lists weekly didactics, GI Grand Rounds, journal club, M&M, hepatology and IBD conferences. These are public rotation descriptions, not a released lecture catalogue or transferable rotations.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Gastroenterology Certification Examination
medical.boardStatus: ABIM has a distinct Gastroenterology subspecialty certification examination. The Johns Hopkins directory labels the programme ACGME Accredited. This independent curriculum is not an ABIM or ACGME programme and conveys no credential.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABIM—not this course—sets eligibility. At application ABIM requires prior ABIM Internal Medicine certification, requisite accredited fellowship, demonstrated clinical competence/procedural skills/moral and ethical behavior, a valid unrestricted unchallenged medical license, and a passing examination. ABIM lists 36 months total fellowship training with 18 months clinical training and diagnostic/therapeutic upper and lower endoscopy for standard GI certification. Training outside an accredited U.S./Canadian programme is not credited. This course cannot supply fellowship months, continuity clinic, case/procedure logs, supervisor attestations, competence, license, examination access, ABIM eligibility, or privileges. Source: https://www.abim.org/certification/policies/internal-medicine-subspecialty-policies/gastroenterology/

officialProgrammes.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / The Johns Hopkins Hospital
officialProgrammes.name: Gastroenterology Fellowship Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: This is an actual separate ACGME-accredited programme, not a generic directory category. The current programme curriculum page is https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/gastroenterology-hepatology/education-training/gastroenterology-fellowship. Johns Hopkins describes a clinical three-year track and a research three-year track; both share year-one inpatient GI consults at The Johns Hopkins Hospital and Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center, inpatient endoscopy, and inpatient hepatology. The clinical track’s later years include limited inpatient rotations, outpatient endoscopy, continuity and subspecialty clinics, clinical research and mentoring. The research track limits years two/three to four weeks of inpatient rotations, with protected research time plus one half-day each of outpatient endoscopy, subspecialty and continuity clinic. The directory record separately lists 3-year clinical-scholar/physician-scientist and 4-year clinical-investigator durations; the current curriculum page does not map that 4-year label to either of its two stated 3-year tracks, so the discrepancy is preserved rather than resolved by inference. The page also lists weekly didactics, GI Grand Rounds, journal club, M&M, hepatology and IBD conferences. These are public rotation descriptions, not a released lecture catalogue or transferable rotations.

medical.programmeSourceScope: MED-032 is scoped only to the one separately named Johns Hopkins Gastroenterology Fellowship Program declared in the item packet. It is not a category entry. The Johns Hopkins research versus clinical tracks are variants within that one programme; neither has been represented as a separate board credential. The ACGME optional GI/transplant-hepatology pathway is a different formal pathway with additional requirements and is not claimed for Johns Hopkins here because this public programme page does not state it offers that pathway.
sourceCaveats: The item packet’s original directory URL and the current Johns Hopkins curriculum URL were both read. The directory is authoritative for programme identity/accreditation label; the curriculum page is authoritative for publicly described tracks/rotations.

The directory lists 3-year clinical-scholar/physician-scientist and 4-year clinical-investigator durations, while the current curriculum page labels both its Clinical and Research tracks three years. The current page does not map the 4-year directory label to a current track; no reconciliation or additional variant is invented.

Public programmes do not release a complete didactic catalogue or transferable clinical case log. No Hopkins rotation, conference attendance, clinical experience, or procedure has been claimed for a self-study learner.

originalClipPlan.title: Original recorded-lecture series: Clinical reasoning, safety, and the GI consultation
objectives: Build a problem representation that separates emergency stabilization, diagnostic uncertainty, and longitudinal management.
Use the ABIM task framework: diagnosis/testing, treatment/care decisions, risk/prognosis/epidemiology, and pathophysiology.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Six short segments: task framework; triage versus diagnosis; evidence hierarchy; equity; uncertainty; fictional consult debrief.

originalClipPlan.title: Original recorded-lecture series: Endoscopy, periprocedural issues, and GI bleeding
objectives: Explain indications, timing, medication considerations, sedation-related risks, and quality principles without claiming procedural competence.
Prioritize stabilization and risk assessment in a fictional overt GI bleeding presentation.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Segmented simulation lecture: indications, consent, preparation, adverse-event recognition, bleeding algorithms, and quality metrics; no procedure demonstration or performance instruction.

originalClipPlan.title: Original recorded-lecture series: Esophageal and upper-GI mucosal disorders
objectives: Compare reflux, Barrett esophagus, eosinophilic esophagitis, dysphagia, food impaction, and peptic ulcer presentations.
Interpret why symptom response alone may not be sufficient to assess chronic EoE response.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Mechanism-to-case sequence on dysphagia, GERD, EoE, ulcer disease, and H. pylori with guideline date labels.

originalClipPlan.title: Original recorded-lecture series: Inflammatory bowel disease and immune-mediated disease
objectives: Differentiate Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis by pattern, complications, monitoring goals, and treatment-risk discussions.
Recognize acute severe UC as a time-sensitive syndrome requiring multidisciplinary supervised care.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Crohn, UC, severe colitis, infection exclusion, monitoring, treatment-risk discussion, and shared-decision communication using fictional cases.

originalClipPlan.title: Original recorded-lecture series: Motility and disorders of gut–brain interaction
objectives: Classify esophageal, gastric, small-bowel, colonic, and anorectal motility problems at a conceptual level.
Use a positive, respectful approach to disorders of gut–brain interaction while screening for alarm features.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Motility testing concepts, IBS and functional dyspepsia, alarm screening, behavioral care framing, and bias-aware communication.

originalClipPlan.title: Original recorded-lecture series: Neoplasia, screening, surveillance, and inherited risk
objectives: Relate colorectal, esophageal, gastric, small-bowel, pancreatic, biliary, liver, and neuroendocrine neoplasia to the blueprint.
Explain why surveillance recommendations depend on indication, findings, family history, quality, and current guidance.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Screening/surveillance reasoning, report quality, inherited-risk referral questions, and neoplasia differential workshop.

originalClipPlan.title: Original recorded-lecture series: Liver disease and hepatology integration
objectives: Organize acute and chronic liver disease by etiology, severity, portal-hypertension complications, and transplant boundary.
Interpret why liver disease is 20% of the ABIM GI certification blueprint but does not make this course a transplant-hepatology fellowship.
originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Etiology-to-complication liver sequence; portal hypertension and acute decompensation concepts; explicit separation from transplant-hepatology training.

originalClipPlan.title: Original recorded-lecture series: Pancreas and biliary tract
objectives: Differentiate acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, pancreatic insufficiency, gallbladder disease, and bile-duct disease.

originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Acute/chronic pancreas and biliary concepts, imaging limits, urgent cholangitis cues, and ERCP credentialing boundary.

originalClipPlan.title: Original recorded-lecture series: Nutrition, malabsorption, and obesity care
objectives: Recognize malnutrition, micronutrient issues, malabsorption, enteral/parenteral nutrition concepts, and obesity-care boundaries.

originalClipPlan.scriptOutline: Malabsorption, micronutrients, frailty, enteral/parenteral concepts, and multidisciplinary nutrition boundary.

medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient presents with overt hematemesis and hypotension. Which framing best reflects the first learning priority?

options.text: Memorize a surveillance interval.
Stabilization and risk assessment while defining the bleeding source and need for supervised urgent care.
Assume peptic ulcer disease without assessment.
Schedule outpatient motility testing.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM places GI bleeding within procedures/periprocedural issues, and ACGME requires competence in GI emergencies and GI bleeding. The question teaches prioritization, not a real-person treatment order.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional treatment-naive adult has confirmed H. pylori infection and antibiotic susceptibility is unknown. Which statement matches the 2024 ACG guideline summary?

options.text: Seven-day clarithromycin triple therapy is always preferred.
Fourteen-day bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred regimen when susceptibility is unknown.
No test-of-cure is needed after symptoms improve.
Antibiotics should be withheld in all cases.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACG guideline states that 14-day bismuth quadruple therapy is preferred when susceptibility is unknown and highlights universal post-treatment test-of-cure. This is educational content, not a prescription.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with eosinophilic esophagitis reports fewer symptoms after therapy. What is the most defensible learning conclusion?

options.text: Symptoms alone establish histologic remission.
Longitudinal assessment may include clinical, endoscopic, and histologic response; symptoms alone are insufficient.
All therapy must stop immediately.
Dilation replaces anti-inflammatory assessment in every case.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2025 ACG guideline recommends monitoring with clinical, endoscopic, and histologic assessments and addresses both inflammatory and fibrostenotic disease.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is consistent with the 2025 ACG Crohn disease guideline discussion?

options.text: Oral mesalamine is proven to induce remission and mucosal healing in active Crohn disease.
Risk of progression and objective inflammatory findings should inform management; symptom relief alone can be inadequate in higher-risk disease.
All asymptomatic Crohn disease requires the same therapy.
Crohn disease is outside a GI fellowship curriculum.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline describes risk factors for progression and emphasizes objective indicators of inflammation; it notes evidence does not support oral mesalamine for active Crohn disease.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional hospitalized adult with acute severe ulcerative colitis, which paired action is supported by the 2025 ACG guideline?

options.text: Avoid C. difficile testing and withhold VTE prophylaxis.
Test for C. difficile and provide pharmacologic DVT prophylaxis unless contraindicated.
Use routine broad-spectrum antibiotics for every patient.
Delay any assessment for toxic megacolon.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline recommends C. difficile testing and pharmacologic DVT prophylaxis in acute severe UC, while recommending against routine broad-spectrum antibiotics.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which colonoscopy-preparation principle is supported by the 2025 U.S. Multi-Society Task Force consensus?

options.text: A split-dose regimen is recommended for most patients.
Preparation adequacy need not be tracked.
All dietary restriction must begin two weeks before colonoscopy.
A same-day regimen is preferred for every morning procedure.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The consensus recommends split-dose preparation; it also recommends tracking adequacy and states same-day preparation is inferior for morning procedures.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has acute pancreatitis and diagnostic uncertainty persists after initial assessment. Which interpretation matches the 2024 ACG highlight?

options.text: CT is required immediately in every patient.
CT is reserved for uncertain diagnosis or failure to improve in 48–72 hours; ultrasound is part of initial assessment.
Imaging is never useful.
ERCP is an automatic treatment for all acute pancreatitis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACG highlight advises ultrasound initially and reserves CT in the stated settings. It identifies ERCP within 24 hours when pancreatitis is complicated by cholangitis, not for every presentation.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the scope boundary for ERCP learning in this independent course?

options.text: Watching lectures confers independent ERCP privileges.
The course can teach indications and evidence concepts, but ERCP performance requires formal clinical experience, supervision, and documented proficiency.
ERCP has no place in GI training.
A fixed video count establishes procedural competence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME requires formal instruction/clinical experience and direct supervision until proficiency is documented; it also says competence assessment is not based solely on procedure numbers.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which ABIM blueprint category carries the largest stated content-category target for the Fall 2026 Gastroenterology Certification Examination?

options.text: Nutrition, 4%.
Motility Disorders, 5%.
Liver Disorders, 20%.
Esophageal Disorders, 7%.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The January 2026 blueprint lists Liver Disorders at 20%, the largest content-category target. Blueprint weighting guides study emphasis; it is not an eligibility rule.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which item is required by ABIM policy in addition to passing the Gastroenterology Certification Examination?

options.text: Completion of this independent course.
Prior ABIM Internal Medicine certification, requisite accredited fellowship training, clinical competence, and a valid unrestricted unchallenged medical license.
A minimum number of streamed-video hours.
Membership in a professional society.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM sets those certification requirements. This self-study curriculum does not fulfill any training, competence, licensing, or examination requirement.

knowledge: Internal Medicine history, examination, physiology, pharmacology, microbiology, pathology, biostatistics, and evidence appraisal.

prerequisites.actualTrainingBoundary: For entry into an ACGME-accredited GI fellowship, the 2026 ACGME requirements require qualifying prior clinical education and specify completion of a qualifying Internal Medicine programme (subject to defined exceptions). objectives: Use the January 2026 ABIM GI blueprint to prioritize adult GI study while distinguishing exam content from training standards.
Reason through diagnosis, testing, treatment decisions, risk, and basic science across GI, liver, pancreas/biliary disease, nutrition, and procedures.

Describe official BIDMC variants accurately without merging their accreditation, procedures, or credential boundaries.
Use authentic de-identified cases lawfully and identify when direct supervision, licensed care, or a current guideline is required.

units.title: Scope, patient safety, and procedural reasoning
objectives: Distinguish an ABIM content blueprint from ACGME training standards, an institutional rotation description, and this independent study plan.
Apply indication, timing, medication-management, sedation, adverse-event, quality, and informed-consent reasoning to a structured pre-procedure vignette.
boardDomains: ABIM tasks: diagnosis/testing, treatment/care decisions, risk assessment

units.title: Esophageal and foregut disorders
objectives: Form a differential for dysphagia, reflux symptoms, food impaction, and suspected Barrett esophagus, then choose an initial test with limitations.
Interpret the role and limits of high-resolution manometry and endoscopic assessment without confusing educational image review with patient-specific diagnosis.
units.casePractice: Compare two authentic, link-only Radiopaedia GI quiz cases; record the differential, key missing data, and when to seek supervised review.
units.assessment: One-page testing-and-management map for a fictional dysphagia case; identify two unsafe assumptions.

units.title: Upper-GI and gastric/duodenal disorders
objectives: Use clinical presentation, test characteristics, and guideline timing to reason through upper-GI bleeding and H. pylori eradication verification.
Differentiate dyspepsia, ulcer disease, gastric outlet symptoms, and gastroparesis while naming red flags and diagnostic limits.
units.casePractice: Work an original fictional post-treatment H. pylori result-timing case; no dose prescribing and no individualized treatment plan.
units.assessment: Ten-question formative quiz plus a two-minute verbal explanation of why symptoms do not establish eradication.

units.title: Inflammatory and immune-mediated intestinal disease
objectives: Risk-stratify Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis using objective inflammation, phenotype, complications, patient goals, and safety constraints.
Explain why nutritional intervention and pharmacotherapy are complementary and why guideline recommendations must be dated.
boardDomains: ABIM Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Other Immune-Related Disorders (10%)
units.casePractice: Create a de-identified problem representation for a fictional IBD flare and list objective data needed before escalating care; use no real charts.
units.assessment: Structured evidence table: claim, population, outcome, dated guideline source, and applicability caveat.

units.title: Motility and disorders of gut–brain interaction
objectives: Select and interpret—not perform—appropriate physiologic tests for esophageal, gastric, anorectal, and colonic symptom patterns.
Use a biopsychosocial, non-stigmatizing approach to IBS, functional dyspepsia, chronic nausea/vomiting, constipation, and pelvic-floor symptoms.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional symptom-and-test timeline to identify alarm features, test limitations, and a communication statement that avoids implying symptoms are “all in the head.”
units.assessment: Interpretation worksheet with a deliberately incomplete manometry report; score is based on limitations and next-information requests.

units.title: Small bowel, colon, diarrhea, and acute lower-GI presentations
objectives: Construct a mechanism-based differential for chronic diarrhea, obstruction, diverticular complications, microscopic colitis, and SIBO-like symptoms.
Explain where capsule/deep enteroscopy fits in evaluation and state its procedural/safety boundaries.
units.casePractice: Link to an authentic, de-identified TCIA CT collection only to practice structured image-description vocabulary; never download, annotate, or re-identify data for a patient-care claim.
units.assessment: Differential-and-testing matrix for a fictional chronic-diarrhea referral.

units.title: GI neoplasia, surveillance, and small-bowel/pancreaticobiliary lesions
objectives: Relate lesion characteristics, family history, pathology, and diagnostic uncertainty to a surveillance/diagnostic reasoning plan.
Recognize when a video demonstration cannot establish competence in polypectomy, EMR, EUS, ERCP, or cancer staging.
units.casePractice: Review the HCC-TACE-SEG TCIA collection only as a licensed, de-identified imaging/data resource; formulate imaging questions, not a treatment recommendation.
units.assessment: Lesion-risk reasoning memo with explicit “cannot conclude” statements and referral triggers.

units.title: Pancreas and biliary tract disorders
objectives: Apply diagnostic criteria and initial evaluation principles to acute pancreatitis and distinguish biliary obstruction from malignant and benign differentials.
Explain why ERCP/EUS are supervised advanced procedures rather than skills acquired from video viewing.
boardDomains: ABIM Pancreas and Biliary Tract Disorders (9.5%)
units.casePractice: Use the CC BY 3.0 Pancreas-CT collection link to practice descriptive anatomy and segmentation awareness. It is not a diagnostic test set and no scan is rehosted here.
units.assessment: Original two-part acute-pancreatitis diagnostic-criteria question plus an imaging-selection rationale.

units.title: Hepatology foundations and chronic liver disease
objectives: Organize abnormal liver tests and chronic liver disease into hepatocellular, cholestatic, synthetic-function, and fibrosis-risk questions.

Use dated, authoritative guidance to evaluate MASLD, alcohol-associated liver disease, viral hepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, and medication/supplement injury without overclaiming from old lectures.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional liver-test trend table and classify uncertainty; do not use a real patient panel or provide individual treatment advice.
units.assessment: Five-source literature update: mark guidance publication date and specify what would require re-checking before clinical application.

units.title: Portal hypertension, decompensation, HCC, and transplant hepatology boundaries
objectives: Explain why ascites, encephalopathy, and portal-hypertensive bleeding are decompensation landmarks and identify multidisciplinary/transplant-referral questions.
Distinguish general GI board content from the separate ABIM Transplant Hepatology certification pathway and supervised transplant clinical training.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional decompensation timeline to identify urgent evaluation questions and scope boundaries. No transplant-listing decision or UNOS certification is represented.
units.assessment: Short-answer board-boundary check plus a referral/escalation reasoning map.

units.title: Nutrition, malabsorption, intestinal failure, and equitable care
objectives: Screen for nutritional risk and explain the distinct roles of oral, enteral, and parenteral support at a conceptual level.
Apply IBD diet guidance cautiously, account for strictures and food insecurity, and avoid prescriptive diet advice outside supervised clinical care.
units.casePractice: Build a fictional nutrition-risk assessment that identifies data gaps and the need for registered-dietitian and treating-team review.
units.assessment: Nutritional-support matching exercise that penalizes unsupported certainty.

units.title: Advanced endoscopy exposure, quality improvement, and integrative case conference
objectives: Synthesize symptom, endoscopic, pathologic, laboratory, and imaging evidence while separating interpretation from procedural competence.
Audit a case conclusion for bias, missing safety data, patient preferences, access constraints, and need for attending/specialist supervision.
units.casePractice: Facilitator-reviewed fictional morbidity-and-quality case. Do not practice endoscopy, EUS, ERCP, anesthesia, or biopsy without an accredited programme and direct supervision.
units.assessment: Capstone evidence-and-quality conference note (1,200 words maximum) with source dates, differential, safety constraints, and scope statement.

assignment.title: Source-dated GI case-and-guideline portfolio
deliverables: Eight fictional, de-identified case problem representations spanning at least six blueprint categories.
For each: differential, missing data, safety/urgency flags, dated primary-source links, and a statement of what cannot be concluded.
One link-only authentic case-resource review with license/attribution field; no image copying, uploading, rehosting, or synthetic “patient scan.”
One final 1,200-word quality/equity reflection that distinguishes video learning from supervised procedure/clinical training.
assignment.gradingGuide: 40% source/date accuracy; 25% diagnostic and safety reasoning; 20% uncertainty, equity and scope boundaries; 15% lawful case-resource attribution. This is formative educational assessment, not a clinical competency sign-off.

formative: Unit worksheets, one guideline-date audit, and an instructor/peer discussion only where a qualified facilitator is available.
assessment.summativePlan: Portfolio pass standard: all source links/updates documented and no unsafe claim of procedural, licensure, certification, or patient-specific competence. No score predicts ABIM performance.
assessment.proceduralBoundary: No simulation, video watching, or self-reported case count is counted as procedural competence.

studyHours.type: transparent independent-study plan, not official programme time
studyHours.note: The 36-hour floor is met only by observed-duration public recordings. Rotations, reading, unknown-duration resources, planned clips, and clinical work are not counted as ready video hours.

mapping.name: Gastroenterology Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: The official page describes a three-year ACGME Gastroenterology fellowship: first year clinical/procedure centers; remaining training tailored to clinician-educator, clinical-investigator, or laboratory-investigator goals. The linked 2025 brochure gives an illustrative, variable rotation distribution: F1 continuity clinic/endoscopy, 8.5 months inpatient consults, 3 months hepatology; F2 six weeks each of consults and hepatology plus research; F3 1.5 months each advanced endoscopy and advanced hepatology, outpatient subspecialty time, consults and research/elective. These are rotations, not recorded lecture hours.

mapping.name: Advanced Endoscopy Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: The page describes usually one year (some pursue additional clinical/research time), two ASGE-matched positions requiring prior GI fellowship, and focused exposure to ERCP (including altered anatomy/cholangioscopy), diagnostic/interventional EUS, EMR, stents, early neoplasia and selected new techniques. It does not state ACGME accreditation or an ABIM advanced-endoscopy certification; do not infer either.

mapping.name: Advanced Hepatology Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: The page describes one year of daily clinical care in advanced liver disease/transplantation with expected clinical or basic research; applicants are graduates of Internal Medicine residency. It is a named BIDMC fellowship but its page does not label it an ACGME programme or an ABIM certification pathway.

mapping.name: Celiac Disease Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Officially 1–3 years and unfunded at the page’s update; it is reviewed/recognized by BIDMC’s General Education Committee. Core work is one-to-one outpatient Celiac Center training, with electives in general GI, IBD, endoscopy, motility, pathology and pediatric GI; no nights/weekends are listed. This is not presented as ACGME-accredited or as a separate ABIM certificate.

mapping.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: BIDMC describes formal structured IBD training and mentorship in pharmacologic therapies, imaging and molecular markers for academic gastroenterology careers; the page says it is reviewed/recognized by the BIDMC General Education Committee. It does not claim ACGME accreditation or an independent board certificate.

mapping.name: Transplant Hepatology Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Officially a one-year ACGME-accredited programme with inpatient and outpatient transplant/advanced-liver experience, liver biopsy and endoscopy exposure, supervision/teaching, transplant observations and quality improvement. BIDMC states it may be fourth-year training after GI or a three-year combined GI–Transplant Hepatology internal pathway. ABIM policy—not this study—sets examination eligibility.

mapping.name: Women’s Digestive Health Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: The official page describes a one-year programme after ACGME-accredited GI fellowship: outpatient, multidisciplinary experience in IBD, IBS, celiac disease, steatotic liver disease, cancer genetics, pregnancy/rheumatologic GI issues, pelvic floor and functional disorders; it includes monthly/quarterly multidisciplinary meetings and a research project. It does not claim a separate ACGME programme or ABIM certificate.

medical.trackType: BIDMC directory category; independent adult gastroenterology self-study scope (not a separate fellowship or credential)
boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) Gastroenterology Certification
ABIM Transplant Hepatology Certification (separate pathway; relevant only to the named Transplant Hepatology variant)
medical.boardStatus: No separate board or ACGME programme exists for the directory category itself. The core three-year Gastroenterology Fellowship is distinct from the category and supports the ABIM GI pathway only when all ABIM/ACGME requirements are met. Transplant Hepatology is a separate ABIM certification and ACGME fellowship pathway. Advanced Endoscopy, Advanced Hepatology, Celiac Disease, IBD, and Women’s Digestive Health must not be represented as separate ABIM certifications on the evidence reviewed.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This is independent study only. It confers no affiliation, credit, accreditation, MD/DO training, residency/fellowship equivalence, clinical competence, procedure log, board eligibility, licensure, UNOS authorization, certification, or guarantee of passing. ABIM GI certification requires prior ABIM Internal Medicine certification, qualifying accredited fellowship, documented clinical competence/procedural skills, an unrestricted license, and the examination. ABIM Transplant Hepatology additionally requires prior ABIM GI certification and qualifying transplant-hepatology training/examination; consult current ABIM policy at application time.

officialProgrammes.name: Gastroenterology Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The official page describes a three-year ACGME Gastroenterology fellowship: first year clinical/procedure centers; remaining training tailored to clinician-educator, clinical-investigator, or laboratory-investigator goals. The linked 2025 brochure gives an illustrative, variable rotation distribution: F1 continuity clinic/endoscopy, 8.5 months inpatient consults, 3 months hepatology; F2 six weeks each of consults and hepatology plus research; F3 1.5 months each advanced endoscopy and advanced hepatology, outpatient subspecialty time, consults and research/elective. These are rotations, not recorded lecture hours.

officialProgrammes.name: Advanced Endoscopy Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The page describes usually one year (some pursue additional clinical/research time), two ASGE-matched positions requiring prior GI fellowship, and focused exposure to ERCP (including altered anatomy/cholangioscopy), diagnostic/interventional EUS, EMR, stents, early neoplasia and selected new techniques. It does not state ACGME accreditation or an ABIM advanced-endoscopy certification; do not infer either.

officialProgrammes.name: Advanced Hepatology Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The page describes one year of daily clinical care in advanced liver disease/transplantation with expected clinical or basic research; applicants are graduates of Internal Medicine residency. It is a named BIDMC fellowship but its page does not label it an ACGME programme or an ABIM certification pathway.

officialProgrammes.name: Celiac Disease Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Officially 1–3 years and unfunded at the page’s update; it is reviewed/recognized by BIDMC’s General Education Committee. Core work is one-to-one outpatient Celiac Center training, with electives in general GI, IBD, endoscopy, motility, pathology and pediatric GI; no nights/weekends are listed. This is not presented as ACGME-accredited or as a separate ABIM certificate.

officialProgrammes.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: BIDMC describes formal structured IBD training and mentorship in pharmacologic therapies, imaging and molecular markers for academic gastroenterology careers; the page says it is reviewed/recognized by the BIDMC General Education Committee. It does not claim ACGME accreditation or an independent board certificate.

officialProgrammes.name: Transplant Hepatology Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Officially a one-year ACGME-accredited programme with inpatient and outpatient transplant/advanced-liver experience, liver biopsy and endoscopy exposure, supervision/teaching, transplant observations and quality improvement. BIDMC states it may be fourth-year training after GI or a three-year combined GI–Transplant Hepatology internal pathway. ABIM policy—not this study—sets examination eligibility.

officialProgrammes.name: Women’s Digestive Health Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The official page describes a one-year programme after ACGME-accredited GI fellowship: outpatient, multidisciplinary experience in IBD, IBS, celiac disease, steatotic liver disease, cancer genetics, pregnancy/rheumatologic GI issues, pelvic floor and functional disorders; it includes monthly/quarterly multidisciplinary meetings and a research project. It does not claim a separate ACGME programme or ABIM certificate.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Primary source: BIDMC directory and GME category pages read in full on 2026-10-07. “Nutrition” is the Division’s name in the directory title; it is not an assertion that the category is a separately accredited Nutrition fellowship. Public pages are used only for what they state. Programme pages rarely reveal complete didactic calendars, procedure logs, every rotation or current funding; missing material is not inferred.
sourceCaveats: BIDMC webpages identify offerings but are not a complete rotation/didactic/procedure inventory. The 2025 GI brochure explicitly says rotation patterns and hours vary.

ABIM’s January 2026 GI blueprint is a certification-exam content specification applicable beginning Fall 2026; it is not an eligibility policy, a syllabus, or a guarantee of testing a particular item.

ACG/AASLD/AGA recommendations are date-sensitive; the learner must re-check current authoritative guidance before any real clinical use. The AASLD ascites/SBP/HRS page identifies its linked guidance as updated August 2021.

Public lecture duration is evidence from public video metadata at one date. Direct links can be removed, changed, geographically limited, or contain views that do not reflect current standards. Older lecture content does not override current guidance.

Only TCIA resources have a collection-level explicit open license verified here. Radiopaedia has a CC BY-NC-SA licence with individual-case attribution rules. MedPix was link-only because reuse terms were not confirmed from its landing page.
No proprietary question bank, leaked examination content, payment flow, protected download, real patient record, or fabricated patient scan was used.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult presents with acute, persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. Lipase is 4 times the upper limit of normal, but no imaging has yet been obtained. Which statement best applies to establishing acute pancreatitis?

options.text: All patients require CT at presentation to determine severity.
Two of three criteria—typical pain, amylase/lipase >3 times upper limit of normal, or characteristic imaging—can establish the diagnosis.
A normal amylase always excludes acute pancreatitis.
Imaging alone is required, regardless of the clinical picture and enzymes.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2024 ACG guideline describes the two-of-three diagnostic framework and suggests reserving routine early CT for unclear diagnosis or failure to improve after 48–72 hours of hydration; this fictional vignette already has typical pain and lipase elevation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient completed treatment for confirmed H. pylori infection and feels much better 10 days later. Which approach best assesses eradication?

options.text: No testing is needed because symptoms improved.
Use H. pylori serology immediately because antibodies disappear quickly.
Use urea breath or fecal antigen testing at least 4 weeks after therapy, with relevant medication holds including stopping a PPI 2 weeks beforehand.
Repeat endoscopy in every patient within 10 days.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACG states that post-treatment confirmation is needed; breath or stool-antigen testing is accurate at least 4 weeks after therapy, PPIs should be withheld for 2 weeks, and serology should not establish post-treatment status. This is an educational timing question, not an individualized treatment order.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult has active Crohn disease with objective evidence of inflammation. Which statement is most consistent with the 2025 ACG guideline summary?

options.text: Oral mesalamine is established as effective for induction of remission and mucosal healing in active Crohn disease.
Risk of progression and objective inflammation are irrelevant if symptoms are mild.
Oral mesalamine has not shown efficacy for induction of remission and mucosal healing in active Crohn disease.
All asymptomatic patients require the same escalation regardless of risk.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2025 ACG guideline discusses the lack of oral-mesalamine efficacy for active Crohn disease and emphasizes risk factors and objective monitoring. A real treatment choice requires phenotype, comorbidities, safety review, patient preferences, and clinician oversight.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult with IBD and a symptomatic intestinal stricture asks whether all fruits and vegetables must be eliminated permanently. Which response best reflects the AGA IBD nutrition update?

options.text: A universal restrictive diet consistently prevents flares in adults with IBD.
Texture modification, careful chewing, and cooking/processing may help some people with symptomatic strictures tolerate plant foods; nutrition advice should be individualized.
Diet can replace assessment of inflammation in all IBD flares.
Parenteral nutrition is first-line for all IBD.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AGA advises a Mediterranean-style pattern unless contraindicated, notes altered tolerance of fibrous foods with symptomatic strictures, and says no diet consistently reduces adult IBD flares. The question tests evidence framing, not a personal diet prescription.

options.text: Nutrition (4%)
Liver disorders (20%)
Motility disorders (5%)
Esophageal disorders (7%)

practiceQuestions.rationale: The January 2026 ABIM GI certification blueprint lists liver disorders at 20%, the largest named content-category target. This is a blueprint fact, not a prediction of a particular exam question.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional person with compensated cirrhosis develops clinically significant ascites. Which framing is supported by the AASLD ascites/SBP/HRS guidance page?

options.text: Ascites is unrelated to decompensation and has no implications for prognosis.
Ascites is a decompensation-defining event, and clinically significant ascites/complications should prompt consideration of liver-transplant evaluation and, when appropriate, palliative care.
Only a video lecture, rather than current guidance, is needed to determine management.
No additional assessment is needed once ascites is recognized.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The AASLD page identifies ascites, encephalopathy, and portal-hypertensive GI bleeding as decompensation landmarks and makes the stated referral consideration. Individual management requires urgent clinical evaluation and current guidance.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which pairing is correctly stated in the January 2026 ABIM GI blueprint?

options.text: Treatment/care decisions 45%; diagnosis/testing 40%.
Pathophysiology/basic science 45%; treatment/care decisions 5%.
Risk assessment/prognosis/epidemiology 40%; diagnosis/testing 10%.
Procedures have no periprocedural content.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM lists task targets of 45% treatment/care decisions, 40% diagnosis/testing, 10% risk assessment/prognosis/epidemiology, and 5% pathophysiology/basic science.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner has watched endoscopy videos and completed an independent case log. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: This automatically documents procedural competence for ABIM certification.
This replaces an ACGME-accredited fellowship if the learner exceeds 36 video hours.
It can support conceptual learning but does not replace accredited training, supervised procedures, program-director competence verification, licensure, or board eligibility.
It establishes eligibility for both GI and Transplant Hepatology examinations.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM GI certification requires accredited fellowship, documented competence, license, and examination. ACGME describes fellowship as graduate medical education with formal program requirements. Video hours are not clinical training.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which requirement is part of the ABIM Transplant Hepatology certification boundary for an ABIM candidate?

options.text: Completion of a celiac-disease advanced fellowship alone.
Prior ABIM certification in Gastroenterology, formal qualifying transplant-hepatology training, an unrestricted license, documented competence, and the Transplant Hepatology examination.
Viewing a transplant webinar and passing this course’s practice questions.
Any Internal Medicine residency without gastroenterology certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM’s Transplant Hepatology policy expressly lists prior GI certification and the other requirements. It also specifies distinct pathways and training requirements. No BIDMC directory label or independent course provides eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional course author wants to place a TCIA HCC-TACE-SEG CT image directly into a paid board-prep PDF without citation. What is the best response?

options.text: Permitted because all online images are public domain.
Use it without citation if the patient is de-identified.

Do not do this without complying with the collection’s CC BY 4.0 and data-citation requirements; link to the source and preserve attribution, while avoiding re-identification and unvalidated diagnostic claims.
Replace it with a generated fake CT and label it as an authentic case.

practiceQuestions.rationale: TCIA states that HCC-TACE-SEG is CC BY 4.0 and requires data citation. De-identification does not erase license and attribution duties. Generated images must never be passed off as patient imaging.
practiceQuestions.domain: Case ethics, licensing, and image authenticity

title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Advanced Fellowship Program
level: Clinical physician fellowship (institution-specific advanced, post-gastroenterology programme; independent-study course is not clinical fellowship training)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Intended level: completed or near-complete gastroenterology fellowship / advanced GI clinician learner; independent learners may study concepts but cannot perform clinical care or procedures from this curriculum.
Working knowledge of adult internal medicine, GI anatomy, endoscopy terminology, pharmacology, infectious-disease screening, and critical appraisal.

For the actual Johns Hopkins programme—not this course—public prerequisites are IM residency plus GI fellowship at an ACGME-accredited institution (or non-U.S. equivalent) and Maryland medical licensure.
Ability to access public source pages and evaluate updates; medication decisions, image interpretation and procedures require licensed, supervised clinical practice.
objectives: Characterize IBD phenotype and verify objective inflammatory activity before escalation reasoning.
Compare current guideline-supported management frameworks for UC and Crohn disease without prescribing to an individual.
Recognize acute, dysplasia, postoperative, perianal, imaging, pregnancy and preventive-care questions that need multidisciplinary expertise.
Appraise IBD guideline and trial evidence, including scope, certainty, update date and limits.
Describe the Johns Hopkins advanced-fellowship curriculum and ABIM/ACGME boundaries accurately.

units.title: Phenotype, mechanism, and diagnostic confirmation
objectives: Differentiate Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, and IBD-unclassified using symptoms plus objective endoscopic, radiologic, and histologic evidence.
Construct a differential for apparent flare and identify when infection, drug effect, functional symptoms, ischemia, or another process must be considered.
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology blueprint: digestive diseases/clinical reasoning; no separate IBD examination domain claimed.
units.casePractice: Linked case: describe the MRE distribution, active features, stricture and negative complications before revealing the Radiopaedia report; then state what data would change management.
units.assessment: Five-item phenotype/differential quiz and a one-page problem representation.

units.title: Activity assessment, monitoring, and treat-to-target reasoning
objectives: Integrate symptoms with CRP, fecal calprotectin, endoscopy and cross-sectional imaging rather than treating symptoms alone.
Design a monitoring sequence that distinguishes nonresponse, loss of response, drug toxicity, and non-inflammatory symptoms.
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology: diagnostic testing, management, and longitudinal care.
units.casePractice: Create an objective-assessment plan for a fictional patient with pain and normal inflammatory markers; label uncertainty explicitly.
units.assessment: Structured monitoring-plan worksheet scored with a checklist.

units.title: Ulcerative colitis: outpatient induction, maintenance, and escalation
objectives: Compare guideline-supported outpatient UC treatment options by severity, prior exposure, safety context, route, and patient priorities.
Explain why steroid-free remission and objective reassessment are goals, while avoiding a one-size-fits-all sequence.
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology: inflammatory disorders and pharmacotherapy.
units.casePractice: Build a fictional treatment-discussion grid that separates confirmed inflammatory activity, prior therapies, contraindications, access, and patient preference.
units.assessment: Single-best-answer questions plus a written rationale for two plausible options.

units.title: Crohn disease: luminal disease and advanced therapy positioning
objectives: Apply current Crohn guidance to phenotype, disease activity, prior advanced-therapy exposure, comorbidity, and patient preference.
Recognize the limited role of corticosteroids and the distinction between induction and maintenance reasoning.
topics: diet as adjunct rather than substitute for appropriate escalation
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology: inflammatory bowel disease, medication safety, and evidence-based management.
units.casePractice: Use the linked MRE case to separate active inflammation from a clinically significant stenosis and list multidisciplinary questions, not an unsupervised treatment order.
units.assessment: Medication-positioning grid with evidence citation and safety-screen prompts.

units.title: Hospitalized IBD and acute severe colitis
objectives: Recognize features that require urgent inpatient, surgical, or multidisciplinary assessment in IBD.
Describe the purpose of stool testing, flexible sigmoidoscopy/biopsies, serial clinical and laboratory assessment, and timely surgical consultation in acute severe UC.
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology: acute care, consultation, and patient safety.
units.casePractice: Fictional inpatient handoff: identify data still needed, red flags, and the team members to notify; no medication dose calculation.
units.assessment: Time-ordered escalation map and two original safety questions.

units.title: Preventive care, infection, medication safety, and patient-centered longitudinal care
objectives: Build a preventive-care checklist that includes age-appropriate cancer screening, skin protection, immunization review, mental health, and medication risk discussion.
Identify why immunosuppression decisions require individualized risk-benefit assessment and clinician oversight.
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology: preventive care, professionalism, and systems-based practice.
units.casePractice: Draft a fictional annual preventive-care reminder list and identify which items need the treating clinician or primary-care collaboration.
units.assessment: Checklist audit; learner corrects three deliberately omitted care domains.

units.title: IBD endoscopy and colorectal dysplasia surveillance
objectives: Explain the roles and limits of high-definition endoscopy, chromoendoscopy, targeted sampling, pathology confirmation, and risk-stratified surveillance.
Classify visible lesions conceptually and identify when multidisciplinary review is necessary.
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology: endoscopy-related knowledge and neoplasia surveillance; this course does not confer procedural competence.
units.casePractice: Review a linked educational case only as a diagnostic-reasoning exercise; do not download or reuse images outside the stated license.
units.assessment: Lesion-description exercise and surveillance rationale with a guideline citation.

units.title: Imaging and pathology integration for complex IBD
objectives: Translate an MRE or CT enterography report into extent, activity, stricture, penetrating complication, and uncertainty statements.
Describe how GI radiology and pathology collaboration informs, but does not alone dictate, the care plan.
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology: diagnostic testing and interpretation.
units.casePractice: Linked Radiopaedia MRE case rID 176305: record findings in a structured template before checking the discussion.
units.assessment: Image-report interpretation worksheet; faculty/peer feedback is educational only.

units.title: Complicated Crohn disease, surgery, and postoperative recurrence
objectives: Distinguish inflammatory, stricturing, and penetrating patterns and recognize the importance of multidisciplinary input for abscess, fistula, obstruction, and perianal disease.
Explain the current guideline concept of postoperative endoscopic monitoring and risk-based prevention without substituting for surgical judgment.
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology: complications, consultation, and management.
units.casePractice: Compare linked MRE and perianal-fistula cases; state why image interpretation must be paired with clinical/surgical assessment.
units.assessment: Fictional postoperative case: identify monitoring and referral questions, not a procedural plan.

units.title: Special populations and reproductive planning
objectives: Explain why preconception through postpartum IBD care requires coordinated GI and obstetric care and current evidence review.
Recognize that pediatric transition, sex-specific care, age, comorbidity, and health equity alter communication and risk-benefit discussions.
boardDomains: ABIM Gastroenterology: special populations, communication, and professionalism.
units.casePractice: Fictional preconception planning conference: list which decisions need maternal-fetal medicine and treating IBD-team coordination.
units.assessment: Counseling-plan rubric emphasizing uncertainty, medication review, and shared decisions.

units.title: Clinical investigation, trials, precision medicine, and evidence appraisal
objectives: Appraise an IBD trial for population, comparator, outcomes, applicability, bias, and safety follow-up.
Separate validated treatment recommendations from hypothesis-generating biomarkers, microbiome claims, and promotional framing.
boardDomains: ABIM/ACGME-aligned practice-based learning and improvement; no proprietary exam content used.
units.casePractice: Critical appraisal of an openly linked guideline/trial summary; do not use patient-level data.
units.assessment: PICO table plus a 500-word evidence critique.

units.title: Advanced IBD practice model, multidisciplinary care, and scholarship
objectives: Describe the Johns Hopkins public training model accurately: outpatient clinic/endoscopy and inpatient service with multidisciplinary education plus mentor-matched research.
Design a de-identified quality-improvement or research question with feasible outcomes and ethical oversight considerations.
boardDomains: ACGME competencies and ABIM clinical competence concepts; not a separate IBD board domain.
units.casePractice: Map a fictional complex IBD referral into GI, colorectal surgery, radiology, pathology, nutrition, dermatology/rheumatology, behavioral health, and research roles.
units.assessment: Capstone care-map and research/QI protocol abstract, explicitly non-clinical and non-identifying.

assignment.title: De-identified advanced-IBD evidence portfolio
deliverables: One structured phenotype/activity problem representation using a fictional case.
A monitoring and preventive-care checklist that identifies uncertainties and supervising-team roles.
A 500-word PICO appraisal of a publicly linked guideline/trial summary.
A source-attributed dysplasia-surveillance rationale or linked-case reflection; no copied images or real patient records.
assignment.limitations: This is written independent-study work, not a medical order set, chart review, procedure log, clinical rotation, or credentialing assessment.

formative: Nine original source-cited single-best-answer questions in practiceQuestions.
Unit worksheets: phenotype, monitoring plan, dysplasia language, imaging interpretation and evidence appraisal.
assessment.summative: Portfolio plus a 20-question learner-authored retrieval plan linked to the published ABIM GI blueprint and current guidelines; no proprietary exam material or pass prediction.
assessment.standard: Completion is self-reported only. No grade, CME, certification, training credit, procedure competence, board eligibility, or guarantee of passing is awarded.

studyHours.suggestedDistribution: 36.648 hours of public recorded lectures; 18 hours readings/evidence appraisal; 12 hours fictional linked-case and worksheet practice; 7.133 hours portfolio and question review. Planned original clips are excluded from this total unless later actually rendered, publicly posted, and independently duration-verified.

mapping.institution: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine / The Johns Hopkins Hospital
mapping.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Advanced Fellowship Program
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Actual distinct one-year post-gastroenterology programme. Public page: applicants should complete ACGME-accredited (or non-U.S. equivalent) IM residency and GI fellowship and hold a Maryland medical license. Clinical time is 60–80% (3–4 outpatient-clinic half-days, 1–2 IBD-endoscopy half-days, inpatient service and surgery/radiology/pathology/dermatology/rheumatology education); mentor-matched clinical, translational or basic research is 20–40%. Weekly IBD meeting, Grand Rounds, journal club and presentations are described. This is rotation/clinical training, not lecture hours.

officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Actual distinct one-year post-gastroenterology programme. Public page: applicants should complete ACGME-accredited (or non-U.S. equivalent) IM residency and GI fellowship and hold a Maryland medical license. Clinical time is 60–80% (3–4 outpatient-clinic half-days, 1–2 IBD-endoscopy half-days, inpatient service and surgery/radiology/pathology/dermatology/rheumatology education); mentor-matched clinical, translational or basic research is 20–40%.
