medical.programmeSourceScope: This is not a generic directory category: Johns Hopkins has a named individual programme page and a separate directory entry. The directory calls its accrediting body “Non-Standard”; the public detailed page calls it a one-year post-gastroenterology fellowship. No current primary source reviewed establishes it as an ACGME-accredited separate IBD subspecialty programme, or as creating a separate ABIM IBD credential. Crohn’s & Colitis Foundation IBD-START is Foundation recognition/support for qualifying PGY-7 advanced IBD programmes, not ACGME accreditation or ABIM certification. Study scope: advanced IBD clinical reasoning, evidence appraisal and multidisciplinary-care literacy only.
sourceCaveats: Johns Hopkins clinical-rotation descriptions are institutional programme claims and are not counted as lectures, nor treated as evidence of ACGME accreditation.
The exact Johns Hopkins directory URL supplied in the packet resolves to an entry that labels the accrediting body “Non-Standard”; the detailed current programme page is used for curriculum details.
ABIM publishes a Gastroenterology certification blueprint. This course maps units transparently to its GI scope but does not reproduce content weights, exam items or claim a separate IBD blueprint.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with established Crohn disease reports persistent abdominal pain, but CRP and fecal calprotectin are normal. What is the best next reasoning step before declaring inflammatory treatment failure?

options.text: Escalate treatment solely because symptoms persist.
Confirm whether there is objective inflammation and evaluate alternative contributors to symptoms.
Assume symptoms prove a stricture requiring surgery.
Stop all maintenance therapy immediately.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Symptoms and inflammation can diverge. Current guidance emphasizes objective assessment (biomarkers and/or structural assessment) before advanced-therapy decisions; other causes may coexist. This is an educational reasoning question, not patient-specific advice.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best reflects the March 2026 AGA living-guideline update for moderate-to-severe UC?

options.text: It issued new recommendations replacing the 2024 guideline.
It found no need to amend the existing recommendations after review of new evidence.
It removed all advanced therapies from consideration.
It applies only to hospitalized pediatric patients.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The March 30, 2026 update states that the panel decided not to issue new or amended recommendations. Scope remains adult outpatients with moderate-to-severe UC.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a person with colonic IBD, when does AGA advice say dysplasia screening should generally begin if there is no PSC?

options.text: Immediately at IBD diagnosis for every patient.
At 8–10 years after initial diagnosis.
Only after symptoms become severe.
After 30 years regardless of risk factors.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AGA advice states screening should begin 8–10 years after initial diagnosis, with immediate screening in the setting of PSC; follow-up interval is individualized by risk.

practiceQuestions.stem: A hospitalized fictional patient has acute severe UC. Which action is most consistent with the 2025 ACG summary?

options.text: Defer endoscopy until after discharge.
Perform flexible sigmoidoscopy within 72 hours, preferably within 24 hours, with biopsies to assess for CMV colitis.
Avoid assessing for toxic megacolon.
Delay surgical consultation until all rescue options have been exhausted for weeks.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACG summary specifies early flexible sigmoidoscopy with biopsies and assessment for toxic megacolon; lack of response or toxicity warrants timely surgical consultation.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is the most accurate about the Johns Hopkins program’s public accreditation description?

options.text: The directory lists it as ACGME-accredited IBD subspecialty training.
The directory lists its accrediting body as “Non-Standard,” while the detailed page describes a one-year post-gastroenterology fellowship.
It is a generic directory category with no program page.
Completion creates automatic ABIM IBD certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The detailed Hopkins page describes a one-year post-GI program; the directory entry says “Non-Standard.” Neither source establishes a separate ABIM IBD certificate.

practiceQuestions.stem: According to the 2025 ACG Crohn summary, which proposition is correct for moderate-to-severe Crohn disease?

options.text: All patients must fail thiopurines or methotrexate before advanced therapy.
Systemic corticosteroids are preferred as long-term maintenance.
The guideline suggests not requiring failure of conventional therapy before appropriate advanced therapy and emphasizes steroid-sparing care.
Mesalamine is recommended for all luminal Crohn induction and maintenance.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The summary describes a move away from requiring conventional-therapy failure before advanced therapy when appropriate and limits corticosteroids to short-term induction; it strongly discourages mesalamine for luminal Crohn disease.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional imaging report describes terminal-ileal short-segment stenosis, mural enhancement, mesenteric engorgement and no collection. What is the most appropriate educational interpretation?

options.text: The report alone determines a definitive medication and operation plan.
It supports structured assessment of active disease and a stricture, while clinical, endoscopic, laboratory and multidisciplinary context remain necessary.
It proves UC because the terminal ileum is involved.
It makes pathology and clinical assessment unnecessary.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The linked MRE case reports active Crohn-pattern findings and a short inflammatory stricture but imaging is one component of care; Hopkins explicitly describes radiology and pathology education as multidisciplinary.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which item is NOT a substitute for ABIM eligibility for Gastroenterology certification?

options.text: Completion of an accredited GI fellowship plus the other ABIM requirements.
Prior ABIM Internal Medicine certification, a valid unrestricted license, competence verification, and passing the Gastroenterology examination.
Attendance at an independent study curriculum or postgraduate course alone.
Required fellowship training completed by the exam deadline.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM explicitly says attendance at postgraduate courses may not be credited toward subspecialty certification. This independent course does not establish eligibility, licensure, procedural competence, or certification.

title: Transplant Hepatology Fellowship Program
prerequisites: MD/DO-level prior knowledge of internal medicine, GI/hepatology, inpatient medicine and evidence appraisal is assumed for this advanced independent-study sequence.

For formal ABIM certification, see the current ABIM policy: prior ABIM gastroenterology certification at application plus qualifying accredited training and other requirements are mandatory; self-study is not a prerequisite substitute.

For the adult Hopkins fourth-year pathway, the programme page says applicants have completed a three-year gastroenterology fellowship. The separate adult dual GI/TH pathway is for internal GI fellows and must meet ACGME/ABIM requirements.
Use only lawfully accessible de-identified material. Do not upload, download, share, or infer from patient records or protected images.
objectives: Reason through advanced liver disease, decompensation, acute liver failure and transplant referral using dated evidence.
Evaluate selection, donor, perioperative and post-transplant questions while distinguishing clinical reasoning from allocation policy.
Map study priorities to the published 2026 ABIM blueprint without claiming that it predicts test content or passing.
Identify immune, nonimmune, infectious and recurrent categories of post-transplant graft dysfunction.
Apply patient-centred ethics, health-equity and evidence-governance principles in fictional educational cases.
Appraise guidance, policy, lecture and image-dataset sources by date, authority, licence and scope.

units.title: Portal hypertension, decompensation, and pretransplant risk
objectives: Interpret ascites, bleeding, encephalopathy, HRS and cardiopulmonary complications as transplant-relevant decompensation.
Prioritize stabilization, prognostic reassessment, referral and palliative-care integration without treating a recording as a protocol.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional decompensated-cirrhosis referral vignette to write a problem representation, immediate safety issues, and information needed for a transplant-centre evaluation; do not make a real treatment plan.
units.assessment: Eight original single-best-answer items plus a cited referral-and-risk matrix.

units.title: Etiologic liver disease and transplant candidacy
objectives: Differentiate viral, autoimmune, cholestatic, alcohol-associated, metabolic and drug-induced liver injury pathways that affect timing, recurrence and candidacy.
Explain why stigma, substance-use treatment, metabolic risk and equity belong in a longitudinal assessment.
units.casePractice: Compare two fictional candidates with different underlying disease mechanisms and list evidence needed to distinguish medical risk from nonmedical assumptions.
units.assessment: Etiology-to-recurrence concept map with source citations.

units.title: Acute liver failure and acute-on-chronic liver failure
objectives: Recognize the distinction between acute liver failure and decompensated chronic liver disease.
Organize an etiologic workup, organ-support priorities and early transplant-centre communication using current sources.
units.casePractice: Complete a fictional ALF transfer checklist that distinguishes recorded facts, unknowns and escalation triggers; no actual patient advice.
units.assessment: Timed short-answer differential and source-trace exercise.

units.title: Liver tumors and transplant oncology
objectives: Use current HCC guidance to frame surveillance, diagnostic characterization and multidisciplinary treatment/transplant evaluation.
Compare HCC, cholangiocarcinoma and selected emerging transplant-oncology indications without treating a historic lecture criterion as current policy.
units.casePractice: Review only linked TCIA de-identified HCC images under their licences, state the dataset limitation, and write a non-diagnostic imaging question for tumour-board discussion.
units.assessment: HCC evidence appraisal and fictional multidisciplinary conference note.

units.title: Candidate evaluation, selection, and longitudinal decision-making
objectives: Structure a medical, psychosocial, surgical, nutritional and goals-of-care assessment for a hypothetical candidate.
Distinguish selection-conference reasoning from allocation policy and from a learner’s independent-study activity.
units.casePractice: Run a mock selection conference with fictional de-identified facts, documenting uncertainty and which question is clinical versus regulatory.
units.assessment: Structured candidate-summary rubric; no eligibility determination.

units.title: Donor assessment, living donation, procurement, and allocation
objectives: Explain deceased- and living-donor evaluation principles, ABO/vascular considerations and donor safety at a conceptual level.
Locate current OPTN policy rather than memorizing a recording’s allocation details.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional donor-offer worksheet to identify consent, transmission-risk, surgical and allocation questions requiring the current policy or transplant team.
units.assessment: Policy-navigation exercise and donor-ethics reflection.

units.title: Perioperative care and early graft complications
objectives: Build a differential for early vascular, biliary and hemodynamic graft complications.
State the role and limitations of Doppler/other imaging in communicating with the interprofessional transplant team.
units.casePractice: Interpret a fictional post-operative timeline and formulate prioritized diagnostic questions; do not infer a diagnosis from a generated image.
units.assessment: Complication differential with red-flag communication script.

units.title: Transplant immunology, immunosuppression, and biopsy interpretation
objectives: Relate blood-group compatibility, allorecognition and immunosuppressive mechanisms to clinical monitoring.
Identify the required training boundary: educational review does not establish procedural/biopsy competence.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional interaction-risk checklist, then cite a primary source to verify a proposed interaction before using it in a simulation.
units.assessment: Mechanism-and-monitoring table and original questions; no prescribing exercise.

units.title: Post-transplant graft dysfunction, rejection, infection, and recurrence
objectives: Separate immune, nonimmune, infectious and recurrent-disease causes of graft dysfunction.
Explain why monitoring, prophylaxis and drug interactions need local protocol and current specialist review.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional abnormal-liver-test timeline to classify hypotheses and choose information needed before escalation.
units.assessment: One-page differential and safety-net communication assessment.

units.title: Long-term recipient care, health maintenance, and quality
objectives: Integrate vaccination, cancer screening, metabolic/reproductive health, substance-use care and kidney-risk monitoring into longitudinal care reasoning.
Apply quality-improvement thinking to a fictional follow-up process without accessing records.
units.casePractice: Audit a fictional clinic checklist for omissions and equity barriers; avoid using any real patient record.
units.assessment: QI storyboard and source-backed maintenance checklist.

units.title: Ethics, regulation, communication, and health equity
objectives: Explain the ethical distinctions among listing decisions, allocation policy, informed consent and donor protection.
Communicate uncertainty, prognostic trade-offs and access barriers in a patient-centred, non-stigmatizing way.
units.casePractice: Facilitate a fictional family meeting role-play with interpreter/access barriers described abstractly; no real patient story is used.
units.assessment: Ethical-reasoning memo with a current-policy citation.

units.title: Evidence appraisal, scholarship, and practice integration
objectives: Appraise a guideline, policy page, lecture and dataset according to source type, date, scope and licence.
Design a research or QI question that respects data governance and does not claim clinical training credit.
units.casePractice: Produce a dated evidence ledger for one fictional question, flagging information that must be rechecked before clinical use.
units.assessment: Capstone evidence brief and oral defence rubric.

assignment.title: Dated transplant-hepatology evidence brief
deliverables: A 1,500–2,000-word fictional, de-identified selection or post-transplant problem representation.
A source table that distinguishes current guidance, OPTN policy, ABIM blueprint, programme description and lecture source.
A one-page differential or decision map that explicitly labels unknowns and escalation to the supervised clinical team.
A TCIA licence/attribution statement if a linked dataset is discussed; do not download or rehost images unless the learner can comply with its terms.
rubric: 10% clear limits and no patient-specific advice
assignment.limitations: This is a fictional academic assignment. It is not a real selection-conference note, medical order, policy interpretation, procedure log, or assessment of clinical competence.

assessment.format: Independent-study formative assessment; no academic credit, certification or eligibility decision.
components: 12 unit checks using the original questions and source navigation
Two fictional case matrices: candidate evaluation and post-transplant graft dysfunction
One evidence-update exercise that replaces an outdated video claim with a current primary source
Capstone evidence brief and oral/self-recorded explanation using the rubric
assessment.passingInterpretation: No score predicts ABIM/ABP performance or certifies competence. Review of a real patient or a clinical procedure must occur only in an appropriate supervised programme.

studyHours.planType: Suggested independent-study plan, not clinical-training time
studyHours.videoClassification: 37 h 33 m 21 s of unique, observed, directly relevant public recordings; all are classified specialty because they address advanced hepatology, liver transplantation, or blueprint domains. No generic common-foundation recording is counted.
studyHours.note: The planned original clips are not films and are excluded from verified hours and suggested total. Clinical rotations and conferences are likewise not converted into lecture hours.

mapping.name: Transplant Hepatology Fellowship Program
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: The official programme page describes an ACGME-accredited, one-year fellowship for physicians who have completed a three-year GI fellowship. It reports supervision by 11 hepatologists; on average six months inpatient liver service and six months outpatient; twice-weekly transplant evaluation clinic; outpatient hepatology specialty clinic three half-days weekly plus endoscopy; research time in outpatient blocks; weekly journal club, research meeting, transplant-hepatology didactics, selection meeting, GI/hepatology grand rounds and tumor board; and monthly liver transplant M&M and pathology. It says fellows lead selection meetings and rounds under supervision and observe procurement/transplant surgery. These are institutional rotations/experiences, not lectures supplied by this course.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Transplant Hepatology Certification
American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) — Transplant Hepatology Certification (separate pediatric pathway; not conferred by this adult programme)
medical.boardStatus: This is an actual, distinct adult transplant-hepatology fellowship programme, not a generic directory category. Johns Hopkins’ programme page states that it is ACGME-accredited and one year long. The ABIM has a separate Transplant Hepatology Certification Examination; the January 2026 blueprint applies beginning with the Fall 2026 exam. The Hopkins directory entry’s “Accrediting Body: Non-Standard” field conflicts with the programme page, so the conflict is retained rather than silently resolved.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Independent study does not provide fellowship appointment, ACGME credit, supervised clinical responsibility, procedural competence, a medical licence, ABIM/ABP eligibility, certification, MOC credit, or a guarantee of passing. For the ordinary ABIM route, the candidate must be previously ABIM-certified in gastroenterology at application, complete qualifying accredited training, hold a valid unrestricted and unchallenged licence, receive satisfactory programme verification, and pass the examination. ABIM describes 12 full-time clinical transplant-hepatology months after GI training; combined GI/TH has separate same-institution requirements. ABP eligibility is separate and requires current pediatric gastroenterology certification. Recheck the boards before application.

officialProgrammes.name: Transplant Hepatology Fellowship Program
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The official programme page describes an ACGME-accredited, one-year fellowship for physicians who have completed a three-year GI fellowship. It reports supervision by 11 hepatologists; on average six months inpatient liver service and six months outpatient; twice-weekly transplant evaluation clinic; outpatient hepatology specialty clinic three half-days weekly plus endoscopy; research time in outpatient blocks; weekly journal club, research meeting, transplant-hepatology didactics, selection meeting, GI/hepatology grand rounds and tumor board; and monthly liver transplant M&M and pathology. It says fellows lead selection meetings and rounds under supervision and observe procurement/transplant surgery. These are institutional rotations/experiences, not lectures supplied by this course.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Discovery result: a real specialty programme, not a directory category. Transparent course scope is adult advanced and transplant hepatology mapped to the ABIM blueprint and to the publicly stated Johns Hopkins fellowship experiences. The official page also describes an ABIM/AASLD-approved, internal-GI-fellow dual GI/TH pathway; it is an institutional training option, not an online pathway. The supplied directory entry is retained solely as a conflicting directory label; no accreditation is inferred from its category field.
sourceCaveats: The public Johns Hopkins programme page says ACGME accredited; its fellowship-directory entry separately shows “Accrediting Body: Non-Standard.” The programme page is used for the programme’s own accreditation statement, and the discrepancy is explicitly reported.
ABIM’s published blueprint is an examination content outline, not an institutional curriculum and not a promise that a topic will appear.

All lecture durations are observed metadata, not estimated content hours. A public link may later change; no video was downloaded, mirrored, enrolled in, or assumed embeddable. Publication dates were unavailable in the observed flat metadata and remain null.
The 5:15:53 immunosuppression course is counted once. Related individual clips from the same event were excluded to prevent double counting.
TCIA datasets are authentic, de-identified research datasets with stated CC licences, but they are not transplant-recipient case banks, patient records, or clinical decision tools.
Medical content was date-checked on 2026-10-07. Guidelines, OPTN policy, labels, and board eligibility may change and should be rechecked at use.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional 56-year-old with cirrhosis develops clinically significant ascites and recurrent kidney dysfunction. Which next-step concept is most consistent with the AASLD ascites guidance?

options.text: Treat the development of ascites as unrelated to transplant referral.
Consider liver-transplant evaluation and, when appropriate, palliative care while managing the complications.
Defer all specialty referral until an allocation score alone crosses a fixed threshold.
Use a lecture recording to independently prescribe a protocol.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AASLD describes decompensation as a major landmark and states that patients with clinically significant ascites and related complications should be considered for transplant evaluation and, when appropriate, palliative care. The question does not set an individual plan.

options.text: Wait for every etiologic test result before contacting a transplant centre.

Classify the patient as having uncomplicated chronic cirrhosis.
Assign transplant status from this limited vignette.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AASLD emphasizes prompt workup, repeated monitoring and early referral/transfer when ALF is suspected. Status assignment is a policy and programme process, not an inference from this educational stem.

options.text: Completion of an online curriculum alone can replace accredited fellowship.

Any unaccredited overseas observership automatically receives credit.
The Johns Hopkins directory label “Non-Standard” establishes absence of accreditation despite the programme page.

practiceQuestions.stem: For an approved combined GI/TH route beginning in 2019, which pairing is correctly described by ABIM?

options.text: 36 months at one institution with accredited GI and TH programmes, including 18 clinical GI months and 12 clinical TH months.
12 months of video study with no clinical training.
A one-year paediatric programme with no gastroenterology certification requirement.
Two unrelated fellowships that can always be combined after the fact.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM describes the three-year combined pathway, its same-institution condition and the stated clinical-month requirements. This course does not confer entry to it.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner observes a public lecture on allograft biopsy. Which conclusion is appropriate?

options.text: The learner is independently competent to perform a biopsy.
The lecture can replace the programme’s biopsy-specimen interpretation experience.
The lecture may support conceptual learning, but accredited training, supervised assessment and programme verification remain distinct requirements.
Biopsy knowledge is outside transplant hepatology.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM specifies training expectations, including interpretation of at least 200 native/allograft specimens, and describes procedural opportunity and competence within formal training. A lecture is not supervised clinical training.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional HCC teaching exercise uses CT images from TCIA’s HCC-TACE-SEG collection. Which statement is most accurate?

options.text: The images are fabricated and may be presented as real transplant cases.
The collection contains authentic de-identified HCC CT data and is CC BY 4.0, but it is a TACE research collection rather than a transplant-recipient case series.
The collection can be rehosted without attribution.
A segmentation label establishes a clinical diagnosis for an individual patient.

practiceQuestions.rationale: TCIA identifies 105 confirmed-HCC cases with pre/post-TACE CT and lists CC BY 4.0 plus citation and usage requirements. Its research scope and licence must be preserved.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which boundary correctly distinguishes the ABP pathway from this adult Johns Hopkins programme entry?

options.text: ABP certification is automatic after completing an adult GI fellowship.
ABP requires current pediatric gastroenterology certification for its transplant-hepatology examination; this adult course/programme entry does not confer that pathway.
ABP and ABIM have identical eligibility rules regardless of prior specialty.
Pediatric certification can be obtained solely through the shared examination tutorial.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABP states that a candidate must currently be certified in pediatric gastroenterology to apply. The Johns Hopkins page supplied here is an adult Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology fellowship description.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional recipient develops abnormal liver tests after transplant. Which is the most useful first reasoning structure for this course?

options.text: Assume acute cellular rejection before considering any other category.
Separate immune, nonimmune graft, infectious, extrahepatic and recurrent-disease possibilities, then identify missing time-course and clinical data.
Interpret a single unlicensed image as definitive.
Change immunosuppressive medication based on a self-study module.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABIM blueprint organizes post-transplant content into immune, nonimmune graft, extrahepatic, infectious and recurrence categories. A structured differential avoids premature closure and does not prescribe treatment.

practiceQuestions.stem: Why should a learner re-open current OPTN material rather than memorize allocation details from a historical video?

options.text: Allocation policy never changes.
The OPTN page states liver distribution policy has evolved, so policy questions require current official-source review.
Allocation is irrelevant to transplant hepatology.
A public lecture can authorize a learner to make offers.

practiceQuestions.rationale: HRSA’s OPTN page explicitly describes evolving liver distribution policy. This is a source-navigation and systems-practice point, not an instruction to make allocation decisions.

components: Three fictional case evidence maps (phenotype/trajectory; MCS intent/safety; candidate/recipient care), each with uncertainty and treating-team escalation language.
One 1,000-word critical appraisal of the linked CC-BY paediatric VAD-to-transplant cohort.
One policy version-control memo using the OPTN landing page.
One de-identified QI/research question; no real patient data.
assignment.limitations: Not patient care, a clinical rotation, an institutional assessment, or a validated exam predictor.

assessment.passingBoundary: No certification, credit, eligibility or passing guarantee is conferred. Review is educational only.

studyHours.plan: 58 total self-study hours: 38.548 verified public recording hours plus 10 hours guideline/PDF reading, 5 hours case/source appraisal, 3 hours fictional case portfolio, and 1.5 hours quiz/reflection. Planned original clips are excluded from completed hours.
studyHours.clinicalHours: 0; clinical rotations and supervised procedures cannot be replaced by this course.

officialProgrammes.name: Advanced Cardiac Therapies Senior Fellowship (public page title: Pediatric Heart Failure and Transplant Fellowship)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Actual separately listed senior clinical fellowship. Public scope includes cardiomyopathy, HF, transplant, VADs and anticoagulation; team care, VAD role, research mentorship and regulatory/programme-development goals. The page does not publish blocks, case minimums, call, protected time, full lectures or ACGME status; none is inferred.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Actual separate Boston programme, not a generic category. “Pediatric Heart Failure and Transplant Senior Fellowship” in Boston’s directory and the assigned ACT senior-fellowship label are naming variants of one offering. Nationwide was reviewed only as an external comparator, not a Boston variant. Public ACT service descriptions are not a rotation schedule.
sourceCaveats: Source pages were read directly on 2026-10-07; public pages/policies and video availability can change.
YouTube durations were observed publicly and counted once by video ID. Publication dates were not independently captured for ledger entries; event year in title was not treated as publication date.
External recordings are not Boston Children’s curriculum. Manufacturer-hosted talks are marked supplementary and not used as sole authority.
No proprietary lectures, protected downloads, payments, private records or fabricated diagnostic images were used.
This course does not state or imply programme accreditation because the public fellowship page did not provide that status; “Non-ACGME” is the assigned item-packet classification.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner says completing the Boston ACT senior fellowship alone creates eligibility for a new ABP advanced-cardiac-therapies exam. Which response is accurate?

options.text: Correct; it is the ABP pathway.
Correct with a VAD research project.
Incorrect; ABP publishes Pediatric Cardiology requirements and no separate ACT certificate is established.
Incorrect only because Boston does not treat transplant patients.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Boston requires prior accredited paediatric cardiology/board eligibility; ABP requires accredited/RCPSC foundation plus verification and examination, not a separate ACT certificate.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is supported by Boston Children’s public fellowship description?

options.text: It publishes fixed weekly block rotations.
It describes cardiomyopathy, HF/transplant, VAD, anticoagulation, team care, research and regulatory/programme-development goals.
It promises independent medical-director authority.
It substitutes for the three-year accredited foundation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The page describes those domains/objectives but not block schedule, authority or a substitute for foundational fellowship.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional child with worsening myocardial dysfunction despite prior therapy, which conclusion reflects the 2024 ISHLT candidate guideline?

options.text: One number automatically establishes listing.
Clinical advanced-HF indicators should trigger advanced-therapy evaluation when consistent with goals of care.
All children undergo the same adult test sequence.
Psychosocial assessment is unnecessary.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ISHLT frames indicators as a trigger for comprehensive evaluation, with paediatric-specific qualifications and family-centred assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which pairing correctly describes a VAD intent on Boston Children’s public VAD page?

options.text: Bridge to decision—support while the team determines next treatment.
Bridge to certification—support until a board exam.
Bridge to unsupervised programming—support until caregiver changes settings.
Bridge to allocation authority—support until fellow changes OPTN policy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The public page names bridge to decision, recovery, transplant and destination/life-long therapy; the other choices misuse clinical concepts.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the most accurate evidence label for the 2021 ISHLT paediatric/CHD VAD document?

options.text: Randomized trial proving one strategy for every child.
Expert-consensus literature review because paediatric comparative trials are limited.
OPTN allocation policy.
ABP exam blueprint.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ISHLT explicitly describes expert opinion/literature review in the setting of limited comparative paediatric trials.

practiceQuestions.stem: A trainee applies the 2025 ISHLT paediatric-HF guideline to all HF related to left-to-right shunts. Key correction?

options.text: It is primarily focused on myocardial dysfunction and not intended for HF related to left-to-right shunts.
It applies only to adults.
It prohibits CHD assessment.
It is OPTN policy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ISHLT page explicitly states this scope limitation.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which competency is explicit in ACGME paediatric-cardiology requirements?

options.text: Independently implant every durable VAD.
Diagnose, manage and refer advanced/end-stage HF/pulmonary hypertension for medical therapy, ECMO, VADs and/or transplantation.
Grant OPTN status.
Complete an ACT senior year to become ABP eligible.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME 4.4.j uses this diagnose/manage/refer language; it gives neither allocation nor independent surgical authority.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional paediatric candidate conference, what is the defensible role of psychosocial assessment?

options.text: Use one score as sole reason to deny transplant.
Identify strengths/opportunities for optimisation with appropriate mental-health/social-work and family-centred assessment.
Replace cardiac assessment.
Determine ABP certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ISHLT says paediatric assessment should identify strengths/opportunities for optimisation rather than reasons to deny transplant.

practiceQuestions.stem: A course author wants to embed a CT image from a free PMC paediatric-LVAD vignette. Correct first step?

options.text: Reuse immediately; free-to-view equals public domain.
Check publisher/figure rights; PMC access alone does not establish reuse licence, so linking is the safe default.
Fabricate a realistic scan instead.
Remove context and reuse without attribution.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free access is not a reuse licence. This course links rather than rehosts the clinical image and excludes fabricated diagnostic scans.
